developers/architecture.html:
Diskarte is one Next.js 16 application backed by three managed services. There is no custom backend server, message broker or job runner: the database does the authorization, the bookkeeping and the scheduled work, and the Next.js server handles rendering, a few HTTP endpoints and secrets.

Technology stack#

Layer Technology Where
Framework Next.js 16.4 (App Router, Turbopack, output: "standalone"), React 19.2 with the React Compiler lint rules diskarte/next.config.ts
Language TypeScript 5 (strict), Zod 4 for every trust boundary diskarte/src/lib/schemas/
Styling Tailwind CSS 4 (@theme tokens), Framer Motion, Lucide icons, Sonner toasts globals.css, experience.css
Data Supabase Postgres (PostgREST), Auth, Realtime, Storage via @supabase/ssr + supabase-js src/lib/supabase/
Media LiveKit (livekit-client, @livekit/components-react, livekit-server-sdk) src/components/voice/
Lists @tanstack/react-virtual for message history VirtualMessageList.tsx
Markdown react-markdown + remark-gfm + rehype-highlight, raw HTML disabled MessageMarkdown.tsx
Push web-push (VAPID) + a database outbox src/lib/push-server.ts
Analytics @vercel/analytics (page views) + a first-party daily visitor count layout.tsx, VisitBeacon.tsx
Tests Vitest + Testing Library + jsdom, PGlite (Postgres in WASM) for RLS, Playwright + axe-core Testing
Delivery GitHub Actions CI, Vercel (production), Docker image for Render or self-hosting operations/deployment.md

Repository layout#

Text
.
├── diskarte/                  The app — self-contained (own package-lock.json, Dockerfile)
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── app/               Routes: landing, (auth), (app)/tambayan/*, settings, api/*, auth/*
│   │   ├── actions/           Server Actions ("use server"), one file per domain
│   │   ├── components/        UI by domain: chat, voice, server, shell, social, profile, admin, ui…
│   │   ├── hooks/             Client hooks: useChannelChat, useDirectChat, useTyping, useSocial…
│   │   ├── lib/               Pure logic + clients: env, security, rate-limit, realtime, outbox,
│   │   │                      read-receipts, push-*, schemas/, supabase/, data/ (server reads)
│   │   └── proxy.ts           The request gate (Next.js 16's replacement for middleware.ts)
│   ├── public/                sw.js, offline.html, icons
│   ├── e2e/                   Playwright specs
│   ├── tests/                 Vitest suites (db/ = PGlite RLS tests), fixtures, mocks
│   ├── scripts/               Brand assets, admin grant, DB readiness check, doc generator
│   └── docs/                  Feature runbooks: web-push.md, voice-preview.md, sql/*.sql installers
├── supabase/
│   ├── migrations/            The whole schema, in filename order
│   └── config.toml            Local `supabase start` settings
├── docs/                      This documentation
├── render.yaml                Render Blueprint (Docker, rootDir: diskarte)
└── docker-compose.yml         Local container + optional LiveKit dev server

The app folder is deliberately not an npm workspace. Render (and Vercel) build with Root Directory diskarte, so nothing needed at build time may live outside it. The root package.json only forwards scripts (npm run dev → npm run dev --prefix diskarte) and runs npm ci inside the app on postinstall.

Request lifecycle#

Every request except static assets passes through src/proxy.ts (the Next.js 16 name for middleware):

The proxy verifies the JWT signature (getClaims()), but pages and actions call getUser() / requireProfile() again because a validly signed token can belong to a revoked session. When that happens they redirect through /auth/revoked, which clears the cookie before /login (otherwise /login would bounce the user straight back).

Frontend architecture#

Rendering. The root layout reads request headers (for the CSP nonce), so every route renders dynamically. Server Components fetch initial data through lib/data/* with React cache() deduplication and the per-request Supabase client, so the first paint of a channel already contains its latest 50 messages. Client Components take over for anything live.

The persistent shell. app/(app)/layout.tsx stays mounted across every in-app navigation and owns the session providers (SessionProviders.tsx):

Text
MeProvider                      who I am (profile, verified flag)
└ AccountPreferencesSync        revisioned drafts / preferences in account_state
  └ PresenceProvider            ref-counted server:<id> presence + speaking broadcasts
    └ SocialProvider            one subscription for friendships + DM conversations
      └ CallProvider            the single LiveKit Room (survives navigation)
        └ SettingsDialogProvider, AudioMixerProvider, MediaViewerProvider, IncomingCallsProvider
          + SessionGuard (device heartbeat), StatusExpiry, ClientDiagnostics, PushSession

Because the call lives above the routes, moving between Tambayans, DMs and Settings never drops a voice call. Settings opens as a dialog (not a route change) for the same reason. The (app) error boundary sits below the providers, so a failing page replaces only the page.

State management. There is no global store library. State lives in:

Kind Mechanism Examples
Server data snapshot Server Component props channel history, server bundle, conversation bundle
Live collections Hooks owning useState + Realtime subscriptions useChannelChat, useDirectChat, useSocial
Cross-cutting session state React context providers MeProvider, ServerProvider, UnreadsProvider, CallProvider
Per-browser preferences localStorage + useSyncExternalStore theme, display prefs, low-data mode, voice prefs, layout widths
Per-account synced state account_state rows with revisions drafts, notification preferences
Durable client queues localStorage keyed by account offline outbox, pending read receipts

Code splitting. LiveKit (~650 KB) loads only when someone joins voice (CallProvider.tsx imports ./live/* lazily); the emoji grid, settings panels, media gallery, command palette and Control Center are separate chunks loaded on first open.

Layout. Desktop uses Discord-style columns (server rail · channel list · main · members) with resizable, keyboard-operable dividers and an optional floating-panel mode on wide screens (WorkspaceProvider.tsx). Phones get a tab bar, a swipe drawer and full-screen conversations (MobileNavigation.tsx). See UI, UX and design system.

Backend architecture#

The "backend" is split three ways, each with a clear job:

  1. Postgres is the source of truth for authorization. Every table has Row Level Security; field rules that RLS can't express (who may change a role, pin, edit) are BEFORE triggers; multi-row operations are SECURITY DEFINER RPCs that re-check the caller. The app never uses the service role for user-facing reads or writes, so a bug in a Server Action cannot widen access.
  2. Server Actions (src/actions/) are thin: validate with Zod, apply an in-process rate limit, call Supabase as the user, and translate database error codes (SLOWMODE, AUTOMOD_BLOCKED, RULES_NOT_ACCEPTED…) into readable messages. Many reads and simple writes skip actions entirely and go from the browser straight to PostgREST, where the same RLS applies.
  3. Route Handlers (src/app/api/) exist only where a server secret or a non-browser caller is involved: LiveKit tokens and webhooks, the push dispatcher and subscriptions, incoming channel webhooks, link previews (SSRF-guarded fetches), GIF search, voice previews, the admin snapshot and health. See the API reference.

Only three server paths use the service-role key: the LiveKit webhook (to broadcast an invalidation), the push dispatcher (to claim jobs from the private outbox) and the one-off npm run admin:grant script.

Data flow: sending a channel message#

A network failure re-queues the entry with the same UUID; if the first attempt actually landed, the retry hits a unique violation (23505) and the action returns the existing row instead of a duplicate. Details: Realtime and message delivery.

Background processing#

There are no worker processes. Scheduled work is plain SQL invoked by pg_cron, plus a database outbox drained by an HTTP endpoint:

Job Trigger What it runs
diskarte-platform-tick (every minute, optional) docs/sql/enable-platform-jobs.sql tick_platform(): publish due scheduled messages, clear expired custom statuses, post due recurring announcements, purge moments expired > 1 day
Push wake (per transaction) trigger → private_push.wake() → pg_net POST /api/push/dispatch claims ≤ 20 jobs, sends ≤ 4 at once
diskarte-push-recovery (every minute) docs/sql/enable-web-push.sql Re-wakes due/expired-lease jobs, queues event reminders, trims 7-day history

Without the platform job, scheduled messages are still published by their author's open tab (publish_scheduled_messages from ScheduledMessages.tsx) and expired statuses are cleared by the owner's tab (StatusExpiry.tsx). See background-jobs.md.

Deployment shape#

Vercel deploys main on push in parallel with CI, so a red CI run may already be live; watch it after every push. Migrations are never applied by a deploy. See operations/deployment.md.

Architectural decisions and trade-offs#

The reasoning behind the larger choices is recorded in Architecture decision records. In short:

  • Database-enforced authorization over application checks — one rule set covers Server Actions, direct browser queries, Realtime and Storage.
  • Runtime configuration (process.env read per request, never NEXT_PUBLIC_* inlining) — one Docker image promotes across environments.
  • Private Realtime channels only — production has "Allow public access" off; every topic is authorized by can_access_realtime_topic().
  • Client-generated message ids — make retries idempotent without a separate dedupe table.
  • Free-tier first — single-instance in-memory rate limits (Upstash optional), lazy-loaded heavy SDKs, a 150 MB Docker image budget.

developers/realtime.title: Realtime and message delivery
developers/realtime.description: Diskarte uses three Supabase Realtime features and one LiveKit feature for live behaviour. Each is chosen for a reason:

headings.text: Rate limits on the send path

developers/realtime.html:
Diskarte uses three Supabase Realtime features and one LiveKit feature for live behaviour. Each is chosen for a reason:

Need Mechanism Persisted? Authorization
New/edited/deleted rows (messages, reactions, memberships, friends, events…) Postgres Changes on private db:* topics Yes (the rows) can_access_realtime_topic() for the join, then table RLS per row
Who is online / in which voice channel Presence on server:<id> No realtime.messages policies (server members)
Typing, "speaking" indicators, voice-preview invalidation Broadcast on channel:<id> / server:<id> No Same policies; clients may not send on db:* topics
In-call soundboard, watch party, games LiveKit data channel No The room token (room members only)

Voice/video media itself is covered in Voice, video and screen sharing.

Private channels only#

Production has Realtime's "Allow public access" turned off, so every channel the app opens must be private ({ config: { private: true } }), and Realtime asks Postgres whether the user may join by evaluating the policies on realtime.messages:

SQL
-- members receive private server/channel broadcasts (SELECT)
can_access_realtime_topic((select realtime.topic()))
-- members send private server/channel broadcasts (INSERT) — never on db:* topics
split_part((select realtime.topic()), ':', 1) <> 'db' and can_access_realtime_topic((select realtime.topic()))
-- plus a restrictive policy: mfa_ok() (sessions that still owe a 2FA code get nothing)

public.can_access_realtime_topic(topic) (latest version in 20261013040000_unreads_mentions.sql) maps each topic to a rule:

Topic Opened by Allowed when
server:<server> PresenceProvider, LiveKit webhook (service role) is_server_member(server)
channel:<channel> useTyping can_view_channel(channel) (membership + private-channel grant)
dm:<conversation> (broadcast) — is_dm_participant(conversation)
db:chat:<channel>[:<thread>], db:chat:<channel>:poll-<id>, db:chat:<channel>:asset:<kind> useChannelChat, polls, workspace assets can_view_channel(channel)
db:server:<server>:events Events dialog is_server_member(server)
db:lfg:<server> LFG board is_server_member(server)
db:dm:<conversation> useDirectChat is_dm_participant(conversation)
db:memberships:<me>, db:friends:<me>, db:dms:<me>, db:mentions:<me>, db:rings:<me>, db:account:<me>[…] shell providers the id is the caller's own
db:broadcasts:<HQ> sticky broadcast banner id is Diskarte HQ and the caller is a member
db:admin:<me> Control Center own id and is_super_admin()

Anything else is refused. Because the join check only guards the topic, Postgres Changes payloads are additionally filtered by each table's RLS for the subscribing user: a member who loses access to a private channel stops receiving its rows even if their old subscription is still open.

Why this matters operationally. CI's local Supabase allows public channels, so a public subscription works in tests and silently delivers nothing in production. Always open channels through subscribeDbChanges() (Postgres Changes) or with private: true, and add any new topic prefix to can_access_realtime_topic() in a migration.

Subscription lifecycle#

subscribeDbChanges(supabase, topic, bind, onStatus) wraps two non-obvious requirements:

  1. Authenticate the socket before joining. It awaits supabase.realtime.setAuth() first. realtime-js copies the access token into the join payload at subscribe() time; a join without it is evaluated as anon, and RLS filters out every row.
  2. Never reuse a dying channel. realtime-js returns the existing channel object for a topic until its removal round-trip completes. Re-subscribing in that window (switching away from a chat and straight back, React Strict Mode's double effects) would reuse a channel that never rejoins. removeChannelSafely() records each teardown and whenTopicFree() makes the next subscriber wait for it.

Join status changes are recorded as session-only diagnostics (lib/diagnostics.ts), visible in Settings → Advanced → Connection diagnostics. They never include message text, ids, tokens or URLs.

Message lifecycle (channels)#

useChannelChat owns a text channel (or one thread): history, the Realtime subscription, optimistic mutations, pagination, the offline outbox and the slow-mode cooldown. DMs use the parallel useDirectChat.

Optimistic updates#

  • Send — the client generates the message id (crypto.randomUUID()) and renders the row immediately with pending: true. The server's row (with server timestamps and author join) replaces it when the action returns. Rows are sorted by (created_at, id).
  • Edit / delete / pin / react — applied locally first, rolled back if the action fails. Edits roll back only if the content hasn't changed again in the meantime.
  • Reactions carry a per-message epoch so a slow snapshot refresh never overwrites a reaction the user just toggled; a message being reacted to is skipped by refreshes until its request settles.

Idempotency#

The message id is the idempotency key. A retried insert whose first attempt already committed fails with 23505 (unique violation); sendMessageAction then selects the existing row (same id, channel and author) and reports success. No dedupe table or request id header is needed. Realtime INSERT events for an id already in the list replace that row instead of appending, and createOnce() (bounded, 500 ids) stops replays from playing a sound twice.

Offline queue#

lib/outbox.ts persists unsent messages in localStorage:

  • Entries are scoped to the signed-in account (userId) and target (channel/thread or DM); sign-out clears this device's queue.
  • At most 50 entries; beyond that enqueue() refuses and the row shows as failed instead.
  • Only text, reply/thread ids, sticker, title and the paths of already uploaded attachments are stored — never files or signed URLs.
  • Flushing is sequential and stops at the first entry that is still offline, preserving order. useOutboxRetry retries every 2 s → 30 s (exponential) while the chat is open and visible, and immediately on online / visibilitychange, because the online event misses short outages.

The 8-bit OfflineBanner shows while offline or while queued messages wait.

Rate limits on the send path#

Layer Limit Error
Server Action (per process) 20 messages / 10 s per user RATE_LIMITED
Database trigger 8 messages / 10 s per user across all channels RATE_LIMITED (SQLSTATE 53400)
Channel slow mode 1 message per slowmode_seconds (moderators exempt) SLOWMODE, detail = seconds left

Missed-event recovery#

Realtime does not replay events missed while disconnected. useConversationRecovery closes the gap whenever the channel re-joins (SUBSCRIBED after the first join) or the browser fires online:

reconcileHistory() only replaces rows that are unchanged since the fetch began; anything edited, deleted or sent live during recovery wins. Deleted ids seen over Realtime are remembered (bounded to 1,000) so recovery can't resurrect them. Results are discarded if the user has switched conversation (scope check) before they arrive. Failures set recovery.problem, which the chat header surfaces with a Retry sync control.

get_reactions_snapshot() reads reactions in one statement, avoiding offset-pagination races and PostgREST's row cap (20261014040000_reaction_snapshot.sql).

Unread state and read receipts#

Channels. channels.last_message_at is maintained by a trigger; channel_reads stores when each user last read each channel; message_mentions stores who a message mentions (only people who can see the channel). UnreadsProvider loads my_unreads() and refreshes it every 30 s in the background (the open server is live via Realtime) and when the tab becomes visible.

Durable receipts. Marking something read goes through lib/read-receipts.ts:

  1. queueRead(kind, id, at) stores "read up to at" in localStorage (diskarte:pending-reads), keeping the later of two marks.
  2. flushReads() sends mark_channel_read_until(p_channel, p_at) or mark_dm_read_until(p_conversation_id, p_at), one flush at a time. Confirmed receipts leave the queue; failures stay for the next try.
  3. Because a receipt names a moment, sending it late never marks newer messages read. The server caps p_at at its own clock. The moment is the later of this device's clock and the newest message's server timestamp, so a phone whose clock runs behind can't save a receipt older than what it showed (which used to bring read conversations back as unread after a reload). Unread is then an exact comparison of two database timestamps (lastMessageAt > lastReadAt); an earlier 500 ms tolerance hid a first message sent right after a conversation was opened.
  4. Mark Unread calls forgetRead() first, so a receipt that hasn't left the device cannot undo the user's intent, then mark_channel_unread.
  5. On databases older than 20261015010000_notification_read_state, the client falls back to the "read now" RPCs (mark_channel_read, mark_dm_read).

The push worker checks the same read state before delivering, so something read on one device is not pushed to another later (20261015010000_notification_read_state.sql).

DM Sent / Seen. dm_participants.last_read_at is readable by fellow participants and published over the existing db:dm:<conversation> topic, so useDirectChat shows Sent or Seen (with names in group DMs) under the latest message you sent. There is no opt-out yet.

Presence#

PresenceProvider keeps one ref-counted presence channel per server (server:<id>), shared by the open server view, the voice call (even while browsing another server) and voice previews. Each client tracks one payload:

TypeScript
{ user_id, status, custom_status, custom_status_emoji,
  voice_channel_id, muted, deafened, video, screen, online_at }

flattenPresence() collapses multiple tabs to one entry per user (newest wins). Speaking indicators are Broadcast events on the same channel, sent on start/stop plus a heartbeat while talking; a claim lapses after SPEAKING_TTL_MS (3.5 s) so a dropped tab can't leave someone "talking".

Separately, SessionGuard sends heartbeat_device() so the Control Center can show per-device last activity (offline after two missed minutes).

Typing indicators#

useTyping broadcasts typing at most every 2.5 s while the user types and stop on send/blur, on the private channel:<id> topic. Receivers expire an entry after 6 s without a refresh. Nothing is stored.

Multi-device synchronization#

State How it syncs
Messages, reactions, pins, edits Postgres Changes + recovery on rejoin
Read state, unread pills, mentions channel_reads / dm_participants via receipts; my_unreads() refresh
Drafts and notification preferences account_state rows with an integer revision (useAccountSync); save_account_state rejects stale revisions, and a conflict never overwrites local edits — the user chooses which version to keep
Profile, status, memberships, friends Postgres Changes on db:memberships:*, db:friends:*, db:dms:*
Theme, display, voice and low-data prefs, layout widths Per browser only (localStorage / cookies)
Push devices Per device (private_push.subscriptions, bound to an auth.sessions row)

Notification generation#

In-app notifications (sounds, unread pills, the mention badge, desktop alerts via DmNotifier) come from the Realtime streams above. Background Web Push is generated in the database: AFTER INSERT triggers (private_push.capture()) on messages, message_mentions, direct_messages, friendships, call_rings, member_warnings and account_controls write outbox rows in the same transaction as the source row. See Notifications, service worker and PWA.

developers/voice-and-video.title: Voice, video and screen sharing
developers/voice-and-video.description: All media runs through LiveKit (an SFU). Diskarte never relays audio or video itself; the Next.js server only decides who may join which room and mints a short-lived token for that one room.
developers/voice-and-video.html:
All media runs through LiveKit (an SFU). Diskarte never relays audio or video itself; the Next.js server only decides who may join which room and mints a short-lived token for that one room.

Rooms and identities#

Room name Used for Who may join
voice:<channel uuid> A Tambayan voice channel Members of the channel's server who are not timed out (RLS hides channels from non-members; private voice channels need a grant)
dm:<conversation uuid> 1:1 and group DM calls Participants of the conversation

The participant identity is the Supabase user id, so every client maps LiveKit participants back to profiles. Display name, username and avatar ride in the token metadata as a fallback for people the client doesn't know yet.

Token issue#

POST /api/livekit/token (route, lib/livekit.ts):

The grant allows join, subscribe, publish and data, only from microphone, camera, screen share and screen-share audio, and forbids canUpdateOwnMetadata (so nobody can rename themselves in the room). Tokens live one hour; that only bounds joining and reconnecting — LiveKit refreshes credentials for connected participants, so long calls continue. LIVEKIT_API_SECRET exists only on the server (lib/livekit.ts imports server-only).

Response Meaning
200 { token, url, room } Join with these
400 Invalid channel / Not a voice channel Body didn't validate, or the channel isn't voice
401 Not signed in No session
403 Not a member of this server / You're timed out in this server / Not part of this conversation Membership check failed
404 Channel not found / Conversation not found RLS hid it (or it doesn't exist)
429 Too many voice join attempts 20/min per user; Retry-After set
503 Voice is not configured on this server LIVEKIT_API_KEY / LIVEKIT_API_SECRET missing

Call lifecycle in the browser#

CallProvider owns one LiveKit Room for the whole signed-in shell, mounted by app/(app)/layout.tsx, so a call survives navigation between servers, DMs and settings.

Key behaviours, all in CallProvider.tsx:

  • Lazy SDK. livekit-client and the LiveKit React components (~650 KB) are fetched on the first join; components that need LiveKit hooks live under components/voice/live/.
  • Pre-warming. Hovering, focusing or touching a voice channel (with real intent, not a mouse sweeping past) loads the SDK and pre-mints a token. A pre-minted token is used for at most 2 minutes; pre-warm fetches are spaced 2 s apart globally so they cannot exhaust the 20/min token limit.
  • One room at a time. Switching rooms shows "connecting" immediately but fully disconnects the old room (bounded by a 2.5 s timeout) and drops its voice presence before connecting.
  • Stale attempts are ignored. Each join has an attempt number; any await that returns after a newer join started is discarded.
  • Room options. adaptiveStream and dynacast are on. Low-data mode captures 360p camera, 720p/5 fps screen share and subscribes to low simulcast layers; toggling it mid-call re-requests remote video at the matching quality.
  • Devices and processing come from Settings → Voice & Video (lib/voice-prefs.ts): input/output device, input profile (isolation, studio, custom: noise suppression, echo cancellation, auto gain), and push-to-talk. Device changes apply live.
  • Push to talk. The mic is published (permission asked at join) but stays muted until the key is held; typing in a text field never triggers it, and switching windows releases it.
  • Presence mirroring. Mute/deafen/camera/screen state is written into the server presence payload so sidebars show who is in which channel; speaking is a Broadcast heartbeat every 2 s.
  • Per-listener mixing. Master volume, per-person volume, local mute, "Disable Video" (stop downloading a camera) and separate screen-share audio volume are kept in localStorage (diskarte:audio-mix) on this device only.
  • Watch one stream. useScreenWatch subscribes to one screen share at a time; others stay listed but unsubscribed to save data.

Call recovery#

Situation What happens
Network blip LiveKit reconnects on its own; diagnostics record reconnecting / recovered
Page reload or a deploy forcing a full reload mid-call On pagehide the tab stores { target, muted, deafened, at } in sessionStorage["diskarte:rejoin"]. A load within 30 s rejoins automatically with the same mute/deafen state
Browser blocks autoplay after a rejoin CallAudio shows a one-click "turn on sound" button
Moderator moves you LiveKit moves the participant; the client follows to the new voice:<id> room
Moderator server-mutes you Your mic publish permission is removed until lifted or you leave
Kicked, disconnected, banned Room closes; the client returns to idle

Vercel deploys change the deployment id, which turns the next in-app navigation into a full reload; the rejoin window exists mainly for that. Batch pushes to main when people are likely in calls.

Ringing (incoming calls)#

DM calls and "ring to voice" pings use the call_rings table (20261004000000_call_rings.sql). Clients never write it directly:

  • ring_call(kind, target, callee?, video?) validates the relationship (DM participants, or fellow server members for a voice channel; never across a block), dedupes already-ringing callees and rate-limits. Each ring lives 45 seconds.
  • respond_ring(ring, accept) lets the callee accept or decline; cancel_rings(target) lets the caller hang up first. Answering a ring older than 45 s marks it missed and refuses it; an unanswered ring otherwise simply stays ringing and clients ignore it once expired.
  • Callees receive rings over db:rings:<me>; IncomingCalls shows the pop-up. Accepting joins the room through the normal token flow.
  • A ring also enqueues a Web Push (call category) when push is configured. Tapping the notification opens the conversation; it never auto-joins.

Voice moderation#

moderateVoiceAction implements Server Mute / Unmute, Deafen / Undeafen, Disconnect and Move using LiveKit's server API (RoomServiceClient):

  1. The caller must outrank the target (canManageMember, the same rule as kicking).
  2. Move only targets a non-private voice channel of the same server (private-channel access is per person and can't be checked on their behalf).
  3. Mute removes MICROPHONE from the participant's allowed sources and mutes the live track; deafen sets canSubscribe: false.

Live voice previews#

Hovering a server icon (or Right Arrow on it, or long-press → Voice activity on touch) shows who is in each voice channel without joining. GET /api/voice-preview?serverId= checks membership, platform ban, MFA and verification, lists only channels the caller's RLS returns, then asks LiveKit for participants of those rooms (≤ 30 channels, ≤ 8 avatars each, bounded concurrency). No token is minted. Full design: diskarte/docs/voice-preview.md.

The LiveKit webhook (POST /api/livekit/webhook) verifies LiveKit's signed JWT and body digest, then broadcasts an empty voice_changed event on server:<id> (using the service role) for join, leave, track and room-finished events so open previews refresh. It returns 503 on failures so LiveKit retries.

In-call extras (LiveKit data channel)#

Feature Topic / module Notes
Soundboard SoundboardPanel, lib/soundboard.ts 12 built-in synthesized clips + up to 24 uploaded MP3s per server. One clip per sender every 2 s; uploaded clips are cut at 6 s; per-listener mute
Activities lib/activity.ts, components/voice/live/activities/ Watch party (privacy-enhanced YouTube embed, drift > ~1.5 s re-seeks), Tic-Tac-Toe, Pinoy Trivia. Whole-state snapshots with a rev counter; newer (rev, author) wins; joiners request a sync
Connection meter ConnectionMeter, lib/call-stats.ts Signal bars from LiveKit quality plus measured RTT, packet loss (delta of cumulative counters, worse of local/SFU view) and jitter

Configuration#

Setting Where
LIVEKIT_URL (wss://…), LIVEKIT_API_KEY, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET App environment (reference)
Webhook destination https://<site>/api/livekit/webhook LiveKit Cloud project settings (same key/secret)
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY Needed by the webhook only; without it previews refresh on presence and foregrounding but may show stale server-side disconnects
CSP connect-src Built automatically from LIVEKIT_URL (both wss:// and https:// origins)

Local development: docker compose --profile livekit up livekit runs a dev server at ws://localhost:7880 with key devkey / secret secret.

Limitations#

  • No recording, transcription, stage/broadcast roles, or end-to-end media encryption.
  • Web Push is an invitation alert, not CallKit/ConnectionService telephony; it can't wake a locked phone into a ringing UI.
  • Physical iOS/Android call behaviour (background audio, Bluetooth routing, battery policies) has not been verified on hardware.
  • Moving a member into a private voice channel isn't supported.

developers/notifications-and-pwa.title: Notifications, service worker and PWA
developers/notifications-and-pwa.description: Per-browser preferences (NotifyPrefs in lib/notify-prefs.ts): desktop on/off, DM alerts, per-server level (mentions or nothing) and mute (with expiry), quiet hours (default 22:00–08:00 when enabled) a
developers/notifications-and-pwa.html:
Notification layers#

Layer Works when Generated by Controlled by
In-app sounds (8-bit cues for message, mention, join/leave, ring) A Diskarte tab is open Realtime events in the client (lib/sfx.ts, Web Audio, no files) Settings → Sounds (master volume, on/off); quiet hours; Do Not Disturb
Unread pills, mention badges, Activity inbox A tab is open my_unreads() + Realtime Server/channel mutes
Desktop notifications (DMs) A tab is open, permission granted DmNotifier watching the conversation list Settings → Notifications → Desktop, DM alerts
Web Push No tab needs to be open (installed app on iOS 16.4+) Database triggers → outbox → /api/push/dispatch → service worker Settings → Notifications → This device, categories, previews, quiet hours

Per-browser preferences (NotifyPrefs in lib/notify-prefs.ts): desktop on/off, DM alerts, per-server level (mentions or nothing) and mute (with expiry), quiet hours (default 22:00–08:00 when enabled) and a one-hour pause. When push is enabled these sync to the account (account_state) so the server-side worker applies the same rules.

Web Push pipeline#

Event categories (PUSH_KINDS): dm, mention, reply, friend, invitation, call, event, moderation, security. Mentions cover @username, moderator @everyone/@here and @{Role name} (moderators only), deduplicated per message.

Privacy defaults. Previews are off: the lock-screen text is generic ("Diskarte") unless the account enables sender/message previews. The outbox never stores message text; each attempt reads the current source row, so deleted or restricted messages are never pushed.

Device registration (/api/push/subscription): the endpoint must be an allow-listed vendor host over HTTPS (validPushEndpoint), the P-256 key is validated server-side, devices are capped at 10 per account and bound to the current auth.sessions row; sign-out removes this device's registration (or all, for "sign out everywhere"), clears the worker's account binding and visible notifications. Permission is only ever requested from the Settings button, never on page load.

Deployment and verification steps: diskarte/docs/web-push.md. Current status: implemented and covered by automated tests; production configuration and physical-device delivery have not been verified.

Service worker#

public/sw.js is plain JavaScript, served with Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate and Service-Worker-Allowed: /, registered by PwaProvider with updateViaCache: "none".

Event Behaviour
install Precache offline.html and the 192/512 icons into diskarte-static-v1
activate Delete other diskarte-static-* caches, clients.claim()
fetch (navigation) Network first; on failure serve /offline.html
fetch (static) Cache first for same-origin /_next/static/*, /icons/*.png, /icon.svg (no query string); keeps at most 150 cached assets plus the precache
fetch (everything else) Not intercepted — authenticated pages, API responses and private media never enter CacheStorage
message: "SKIP_WAITING" Activates a waiting worker when the user chooses to update
push Validates, dedupes (IndexedDB, last 100 ids/tags), checks the bound account, shows the notification, updates the app badge
notificationclick Opens or focuses a window at a validated same-origin Diskarte path; never auto-joins a call
pushsubscriptionchange Defers renewal to the next authenticated page interaction

Changing the precache? Bump CACHE (diskarte-static-vN) so old caches are removed on activate.

Installability and updates#

app/manifest.ts declares a standalone app with start_url / id /tambayan, shortcuts to Messages and Explore, and regular plus maskable icons.

PwaProvider exposes usePwa():

  • captures beforeinstallprompt for an Install button (Chromium) and detects standalone mode;
  • checks for updates on visibility change and when coming back online; a waiting worker shows Update available in Settings → Storage & Data. Applying it posts SKIP_WAITING and reloads on controllerchange — finish calls and unsaved edits first;
  • Clear downloaded app files removes the static caches only; drafts and queued messages (in localStorage) survive.

Mobile behaviour#

  • useAppViewport: the shell is 100dvh; while the iOS keyboard is up it sizes to the visual viewport (data-keyboard, --app-height) so the composer stays visible. The root viewport sets interactive-widget=resizes-content and viewport-fit=cover.
  • Safe-area padding, 16 px inputs (no zoom on focus), 44 px touch targets on coarse pointers.
  • useSwipeDrawer (edge swipe opens navigation) and useSwipeReply (swipe a message to reply); vertical scrolling stays native.
  • Theme colour follows the saved colour mode from the first paint (generateViewport reads the diskarte-mode cookie).

Limitations#

  • Offline mode is a fallback page plus queued sends; past conversations are not readable offline.
  • iOS requires installing to the Home Screen before push can be enabled; Android/desktop support depends on the browser. OS focus modes and battery settings can delay or drop pushes.
  • Badges count unread conversations/channels, not messages, and can be stale on a device that was closed while you read elsewhere.

developers/database.title: Database guide
developers/database.description: The whole schema lives in supabase/migrations/, applied in filename order. This page explains how it is organized and why. For every table, column, constraint, index, policy, trigger and function, see
developers/database.html:
The whole schema lives in supabase/migrations/, applied in filename order. This page explains how it is organized and why. For every table, column, constraint, index, policy, trigger and function, see the generated database reference.

Schemas#

Schema Contents Reachable through the API?
public All application tables and RPCs Yes, as authenticated (RLS on every table); anon has no table privileges
private_push Push subscriptions, outbox, deliveries, attempts, configuration No — only definer functions and the service role
auth, storage, realtime Supabase-managed; Diskarte adds policies on storage.objects and realtime.messages and rows in storage.buckets Via Supabase Auth / Storage / Realtime

Domains and relationships#

The 59 tables group into a few domains. Foreign-key diagrams per domain (the full generated map is in the reference):

Identity and accounts#

profiles is created by a trigger on auth.users insert, from the sign-up metadata (username, display_name). onboarded gates the app until the profile builder is finished.

Communities (Tambayans)#

Messaging#

Social#

Friendships store each pair once as (user_low, user_high) (ordered ids) with a status of pending or accepted; classifyFriendships() turns rows into "incoming", "outgoing" and "accepted" from the viewer's side. Direct conversations have a unique direct_key so a pair can't have two 1:1 DMs.

Platform#

platform_admins (role table), account_controls, admin_audit_logs, system_broadcasts, system_creators, site_visits, problem_reports, user_devices, release_announcements (one row per officially announced release; see release announcements). Diskarte HQ is a system server (is_system, fixed id d15ca47e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001) that every profile joins automatically.

Permission model#

Server ranks live in members.role (member < moderator < admin, the member_role enum). server_role(server) returns the caller's rank and has_server_role(server, min) compares it. The server owner (servers.owner_id) is always an admin and is the only one who can demote admins or transfer ownership. members_guard enforces: only admins change roles; nobody changes their own or the owner's role; only the owner demotes admins; moderators may only rename members below them.

Custom roles (server_roles, member_roles) are cosmetic colours and labels plus a way to grant private-channel access to a group; moderation powers still come from the rank.

Platform roles (platform_admins.role: super_admin or moderator) are checked by is_super_admin() and mirrored into Diskarte HQ as admin / moderator.

Common helper functions (all SECURITY DEFINER, search_path = '', stable):

Function True when
is_server_member(server) Caller has a members row
has_server_role(server, min) Caller's rank ≥ min
can_view_channel(channel) Member, and the channel is public or the caller has a grant (or is admin)
has_channel_grant(channel, server) Admin, or a channel_access row for the caller or one of their roles
is_dm_participant(conversation) Caller is in dm_participants
are_friends(a, b) Accepted friendship
is_platform_banned(user?) account_controls.banned_until in the future
is_verified_user() Confirmed email or phone
mfa_ok() Session is aal2, or the account has no verified factor
is_super_admin() platform_admins.role = 'super_admin' for the caller

Data integrity guarantees#

  • Server-assigned fields. Insert triggers overwrite author_id with auth.uid(), created_at with now(), and clear pin/edit fields, so clients can't backdate or impersonate.
  • Immutable relationships. Guards refuse moving members, messages, events or channels between servers after creation (MEMBER_IMMUTABLE_FIELD and similar).
  • Attachments must be objects in the attachments bucket under <server>/<channel>/<uploader>/<uuid>.<ext>, of an allow-listed MIME type and ≤ 10 MB — checked by the message trigger, the bucket configuration and the upload policy.
  • Counters (thread_reply_count, rsvp_count, last_message_at) are maintained by triggers; event capacity updates serialize on the event row so RSVPs can't overbook.
  • Revisions. workspace_documents, workspace_assets and account_state carry an integer revision; saves with a stale revision fail instead of overwriting.
  • Rate limits in the database: 8 messages / 10 s per user; reports 5 / hour; push registration and tests per minute; webhooks 30 / minute per webhook.
  • Auto-mod drops instead of raising so its audit entry commits (return null from the trigger; the API sees zero rows inserted).

Realtime publication#

30 tables are in supabase_realtime (listed in the reference). Adding a table to the publication is a migration (alter publication supabase_realtime add table …); subscribers also need a topic rule in can_access_realtime_topic() (see Realtime and message delivery).

Storage buckets#

Bucket Public Limit Object path Who writes / reads
attachments no 10 MB; images, MP3/MP4, voice (WebM/Ogg/MP4 audio) <server>/<channel>/<uploader>/<uuid>.<ext> or dm/<conversation>/<uploader>/<uuid>.<ext> Members of the server upload to their own folder and read; DM participants for dm/…; uploader or moderators delete. Served as short-lived signed URLs
avatars yes 5 MB images <user>/(avatar|banner)-<uuid>.<ext>, servers/<server>/… Owner (or server admin for servers/) writes and lists; anyone loads images by public URL, but nobody else can list the bucket
emoji yes 256 KB PNG/GIF/WebP <server>/<uuid>.<ext> Server admins write
soundboard no 1 MB MP3 <server>/<uuid>.mp3 Admins write, members read
moments no 5 MB images <user>/… Author writes/deletes; readable while the viewer can see the moment

A restrictive policy (mfa_ok()) applies to all Storage access.

Retention#

Data Retention
Moments Hidden after 24 h; rows purged 1 day later by tick_platform() (photos remain until account deletion)
Push outbox and attempts 7 days (tick_push()), subscriptions until removed or the vendor reports 404/410
Call rings 45 s of relevance; rows are kept
Everything else (messages, audit logs, site visits, reports) Kept until deleted by a user, moderator or account deletion; no automatic expiry

Account deletion and export#

Other messages authored by a deleted account keep their content with author_id set to null (shown as a deleted user); private data (DMs participation, friendships, notes, devices, push subscriptions, XP, moments, scheduled messages) cascades. export_my_data() returns one JSON document of everything the account wrote or set; later migrations (…_account_export_sync, …_account_data_coverage) wrap the base function rather than rewriting it. Exact coverage is tested in tests/db/account-data-coverage.test.ts.

Writing migrations#

See Database migrations and RLS review for naming, the RLS review checklist and how to test with PGlite. Then regenerate the reference:

Terminal
npm run docs:db --prefix diskarte

developers/security.title: Authentication and security
developers/security.description: This guide explains how identity, sessions and authorization work end to end. The threat model, the full control-by-control table and how to report a vulnerability are in the repository's SECURITY.md;
developers/security.html:
This guide explains how identity, sessions and authorization work end to end. The threat model, the full control-by-control table and how to report a vulnerability are in the repository's SECURITY.md; this page links to it rather than repeating it.

Authentication flows#

Diskarte uses Supabase Auth (email + password, optional GitHub / Google / Discord OAuth, TOTP two-factor). All auth forms are Server Actions in app/(auth)/actions.ts.

Registration and email verification#

Password policy: 10–72 bytes with lowercase, uppercase, digit and symbol (passwordSchema); the live checklist on the form shows the same rules, and Supabase Auth should be configured identically. Sign-in only checks the shape of the input, never reveals the policy, and returns one message for unknown email and wrong password.

Verified accounts have a confirmed email or phone (is_verified_user()). Channels can require verification to post; push and voice previews respect the same gate.

Onboarding (/onboarding): the profile builder sets avatar (salakot preset or upload), banner, bio and status and flips profiles.onboarded. The (app) layout redirects un-onboarded accounts there.

Sign-in#

  • Password: signInAction → supabase.auth.signInWithPassword → redirect to next (validated by safeRedirectPath, same-site paths only).
  • OAuth: signInWithProviderAction only accepts providers listed in AUTH_OAUTH_PROVIDERS, starts a PKCE flow (verifier in a cookie) and returns through /auth/callback, which exchanges the code.
  • Accounts carrying user_metadata.must_change_password (created with a temporary password) are sent to /reset-password?first=1 from the proxy, the login action and every protected render.

Two-factor authentication (TOTP)#

Settings → Account → Two-factor (TwoFactorSettings) enrols an authenticator app with supabase.auth.mfa.enroll, verifies the first code and can unenrol after re-verifying. Once an account has a verified factor, an aal1 session is useless until the second step:

Layer Enforcement
Pages requireProfile() → needsSecondFactor() → /mfa?next=… (MfaChallenge)
PostgREST (tables and RPCs) pgrst.db_pre_request = 'public.mfa_pre_request' refuses every request from such sessions
Storage and Realtime Restrictive policies two-factor sessions only using mfa_ok()
Push, voice preview, account deletion Explicit needsSecondFactor() / mfa_ok() checks

mfa_ok() is true when the JWT's aal is aal2 or the account has no verified factor. The Auth API itself (where the code is verified) is unaffected (20261013160000_mfa_enforcement.sql).

Password recovery#

/forgot-password → requestPasswordResetAction (always answers "If an account exists…") → Supabase emails a link to /auth/callback?next=/reset-password → recovery session → /reset-password → changePasswordAction.

Sessions#

Aspect Behaviour
Storage @supabase/ssr cookies: host-only, Path=/, SameSite=Lax, Secure on HTTPS, not HttpOnly (the browser client needs the token for Realtime, Storage and direct queries; see SECURITY.md trade-offs)
Refresh proxy.ts refreshes on every request; getClaims() verifies the JWT signature
Server checks Pages and actions call getUser() (round-trip to Auth), which catches revoked sessions
Revoked / banned / deleted Protected renders redirect to /auth/revoked, which clears the cookie and shows "Your session ended"
Sign out This device (scope: local) or every device (scope: global, revokes all refresh tokens). Also removes this device's push registration and Control Center device record, and clears this browser's message outbox
Device heartbeat SessionGuard sends heartbeat_device(); banned accounts are signed out within seconds via db:account:<me>

Authorization summary#

Resource Rule (enforced in Postgres)
Tambayan content Members only (is_server_member)
Private channels Admins plus users/roles with a channel_access grant (can_view_channel); applies to messages, events in that channel, search, Realtime topics, push and workspace documents
Moderation Rank hierarchy member < moderator < admin, owner above all; you can only act on members below you
DMs Participants only. Starting a 1:1 DM requires an accepted friendship and no block in either direction; blocking ends the conversation for both
Friend requests Recipient's privacy_settings: everyone, people who share a server (Diskarte HQ doesn't count), or nobody
Platform administration is_super_admin() in the proxy, the page, the action and every admin_* RPC
Banned accounts Restrictive RLS blocks posting messages and DMs even with a still-valid access token

Details and the evaluation order: database.md → Permission model.

Request security#

Control Implementation
CSP Per-request nonce + strict-dynamic scripts; connect-src limited to self, Supabase and LiveKit (both http(s) and ws(s)); img-src self, Supabase, OAuth avatar CDNs, GIPHY; frame-src only youtube-nocookie.com; frame-ancestors 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests on HTTPS (buildCsp)
Static headers HSTS (2 years, preload), X-Frame-Options: DENY, nosniff, strict referrer, COOP same-origin, Permissions-Policy (camera/mic/display-capture self only) (next.config.ts)
CSRF Same-origin Origin/Referer required for non-safe /api/*; Next.js Origin check for Server Actions; SameSite=Lax cookies
CORS Only SITE_URL + ALLOWED_ORIGINS
Open redirects safeRedirectPath() on every next parameter
Canonical host Pages on any other host 308 to SITE_URL (cookies, OAuth and CSRF line up)
Rate limits See API reference → Conventions
XSS Markdown without raw HTML (HTML becomes literal text), protocol allow-listed links, no remote images in messages, React escaping (MessageMarkdown.tsx)
SSRF Link previews fetch only public addresses on default ports, verified at connect time and on every redirect, 512 KB / 5 s caps (lib/ssrf.ts); preview images go through an HMAC-signed same-origin proxy with a sandbox CSP

Integration secrets#

Secret Protects Notes
LIVEKIT_API_SECRET Room tokens, webhook verification, preview-image HMAC (domain-separated key) Server only (server-only import guard + a test that fails if client modules reference secrets)
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY LiveKit webhook broadcast, push dispatcher, admin grant script Never used for user requests
Channel webhook tokens POST /api/webhooks/<id>/<token> 48 hex chars, shown once, stored as a hash; rotate in Server settings if leaked; anon-only RPC; 30/min per webhook
PUSH_DISPATCH_SECRET /api/push/dispatch ≥ 32 chars, constant-time compare, must match Vault diskarte_push_secret
VAPID private key Push message signing Keep stable; rotating forces every device to re-subscribe

Secret management rules: keep secrets in the hosting provider's environment settings and Supabase Vault; never in git, logs, screenshots, issue trackers or NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables. Rotate LiveKit keys from LiveKit Cloud and Supabase keys from the dashboard if exposed, then update the host and redeploy.

File uploads#

Attachments are validated in four places (browser magic bytes, Server Action Zod schema, the message trigger and the Storage bucket + policy), stored privately, and served by short-lived signed URLs from Supabase's origin so uploaded content never runs on Diskarte's origin. Limits and paths: database.md → Storage buckets.

Privacy features#

Feature Where
Data export ("Request all of my data") Settings → Data; export_my_data() returns one JSON file of everything the account wrote or set, including later additions (favourites, scheduled messages, moments, XP)
Account deletion Settings → Danger zone; type your username; files removed first, then delete_my_account() (see Database guide)
Friend request policy Settings → Privacy
Push previews Off by default (generic lock-screen text)
Diagnostics Session-only, no content/ids/tokens; no third-party error reporting is configured
Analytics Vercel Analytics page views; first-party visit count stores a random browser id, no IP or user id
Storage listing The public avatars bucket serves images by URL only; storage.objects rows (and so list()) are visible just to the uploader's own folder or a server admin's servers/<server>/ folder, so user and private-server ids can't be enumerated (20261109020000_avatar_listing.sql)

Privacy hardening (2026-11-09)#

A security review found four ways private information could reach people who shouldn't see it. Migration 20261109000000_privacy_hardening.sql closes them in the database, with client changes to match. Production needs the migration applied by hand (rollback SQL is at the bottom of the file).

Deploy order: deploy the app first, then apply the migration. The new app works against the old schema: a missing privacy_settings.invisible reads as "not invisible", and until the migration voice:<id> topics are refused, so a private channel's occupants briefly don't show (they're never announced server-wide). Applying the migration first would leave the old app unaware of Invisible: it would read your last visible status back and show you as online in your own interface.

Leak Fix Enforced by
Anyone signed in could see who chose Invisible (profiles.status is public), and invisible users' apps still announced them on server presence The choice moves to the owner-only privacy_settings.invisible; a trigger keeps 'invisible' out of profiles.status (others see the last visible status), and a check constraint backs it up. A restrictive Realtime policy refuses presence from invisible users, and the app stops tracking. Voice previews show invisible people as offline profiles_hide_invisible trigger, privacy_settings RLS, "invisible users publish no presence" on realtime.messages
Private voice channels were announced server-wide: every member received their ids and who was inside Occupancy of a private voice channel is published only on its own voice:<channel id> topic, which requires can_view_channel; the server-wide topic carries public channels only can_access_realtime_topic (voice kind)
Moderators without access to a private channel could read its name and message excerpts in the audit log Every audit row is tagged with its channel (audit_logs.channel_id, channel_private); moderators read a channel's rows only if they can view the channel (its current access, so a channel made private later is covered too). Admins see everything; bans, timeouts, warnings and other server-level rows are unchanged. Rows about deleted channels count as private audit_logs select policy via can_read_audit_channel (answers only for the server's moderators)
Moderators could read the full edit history of messages in private channels they can't open Moderators only read earlier versions of messages they can see; authors keep their own history; admins see everything "authors and moderators read edit history" on message_edits (checks the message under messages RLS)

Also hardened: friends around (friends_activity) checks the private invisible flag, so a stale tab still reporting "online" can't make an invisible friend show up; the heartbeat returns your real status so a stale tab adopts Invisible (or leaves it) within one beat; choosing Invisible no longer writes the public profile row at all (not even updated_at); the app only rejoins presence after the server has cleared Invisible, never re-sends an unchanged presence payload (which would time a private call), and LiveKit's "voice changed" signal for a private channel goes to its own voice:<id> topic instead of the whole server.

Residual risks.

  • A voice channel made private while someone is already in its call keeps that person listed on the server-wide presence until they rejoin the call.
  • Realtime checks topic authorisation when a client joins (and when its token refreshes), so a client that was already subscribed when it went invisible or lost a channel grant keeps its subscription until it rejoins. The app untracks the moment you choose Invisible and rejoins once the server confirms you left it.
  • Tabs running a bundle from before the deploy keep the old behaviour (private voice on the server topic) until they reload; the database refuses their presence while you're invisible, but not the private-channel payload, which only the new client keeps off server:<id>.
  • Keeping a private voice channel's occupancy off the server-wide topic is client-enforced: any member can publish whatever presence payload they like on server:<id>, so a modified client could still announce its own private call. It can't reveal anyone else's.
  • The heartbeat compares server time to the tab's clock when adopting Invisible from another tab; a badly skewed clock can delay that until the next reload.

Tests: tests/db/privacy-hardening.test.ts, tests/ui/PresencePrivacy.test.tsx, tests/ui/StatusHighlight.test.tsx, tests/ui/voice-preview.test.tsx, tests/admin/live-session.test.tsx, src/app/api/livekit/webhook/__tests__/route.test.ts, src/lib/__tests__/auth-profile.test.ts, src/lib/__tests__/voice-preview-server.test.ts.

Security testing#

The security-relevant suites are listed in SECURITY.md → Security testing and in Testing. Run them all with npm test from the repository root. When adding a table, policy or definer function, add a PGlite test that attacks it as a non-member, a member and a lower-ranked moderator (see Database migrations and RLS review).

Public repository review (2026-11-07)#

The GitHub repository is public, so everything committed — including Markdown that the Help Center doesn't publish — is readable by anyone. A review of tracked files and history found:

Finding Severity Status
No credentials, keys, tokens, connection strings or .env files in tracked files or git history (pattern scan for JWTs, cloud keys, private keys and *_KEY= values) — .env* is ignored except .env.example; keep it that way
Operational runbooks (docs/operations/*, diskarte/docs/web-push.md, docs/sql/*) describe procedures, job names, Vault secret names and endpoint paths, but no secret values or private hosts Low Acceptable: every privileged path is authenticated by a secret or the service role. Never add values, project refs or customer data to these files
20261005000000_super_server.sql seeds the owner's production account UUID and handle as the Diskarte HQ creator Low A UUID isn't a credential and grants nothing by itself; future seeds should be applied by hand rather than committed
Commit metadata carries the author's personal email Info Consider GitHub's no-reply address for future commits
Unpublished docs are excluded from the Help Center and its search by an allow-list — Preserved (docs/site.json); this is about discoverability, not secrecy

If material ever needs to be genuinely private (incident write-ups with user data, vendor contracts, real infrastructure identifiers), keep it out of this repository — in a private repository or the hosting providers' own access-controlled settings — rather than relying on the Help Center allow-list.

developers/environment.html:
All variables are read at runtime from process.env (never inlined at build time), so the same build runs everywhere. Locally, put them in diskarte/.env.local (copy diskarte/.env.example). On Vercel/Render set them in the project settings and redeploy — running deployments don't pick up changes.

Never give a secret a NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix, and never commit real values.

Required#

Variable Exposure Accepted fallbacks Description
SUPABASE_URL browser + server NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL https://<ref>.supabase.co (or http://127.0.0.1:54321 locally). Also used to build the CSP and image allow-list
SUPABASE_ANON_KEY browser + server SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY Anon/publishable key (≥ 20 chars). Public by design; RLS protects data
LIVEKIT_URL browser + server NEXT_PUBLIC_LIVEKIT_URL wss://<project>.livekit.cloud (ws:// allowed for local dev)
LIVEKIT_API_KEY server only — Signs room tokens, verifies webhooks
LIVEKIT_API_SECRET server only — Signs room tokens; also the root of the link-preview image HMAC key

Missing or malformed public values make pages show a configuration notice and /api/health report "config": "missing"; missing LiveKit secrets report "livekitSecrets": "missing" and voice joins return 503.

Recommended#

Variable Default Description
SITE_URL NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, then RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL, then http://localhost:3000 Canonical public origin: OAuth/email redirects, invite links, metadata, CSRF/CORS origin and the host every page request is 308-redirected to. Set it explicitly on Vercel (stable production domain, not a preview URL). For local runs on another port, set it to that exact origin or API POSTs return 403
AUTH_OAUTH_PROVIDERS unset → github,google; empty string → none Comma-separated subset of github,google,discord that are enabled in Supabase Auth. Controls which buttons appear
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL, UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN unset (in-memory limits) Share the proxy's rate-limit counters across instances. Needed on serverless/multi-instance hosts for meaningful auth limits

Optional features#

Variable Needed for Notes
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY LiveKit webhook (voice preview refresh), Web Push dispatcher, npm run admin:grant, E2E role grants Server only. User-facing code never uses it
VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY Web Push 87-char base64url P-256 public key
VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY Web Push 43-char base64url private key; must match the public key
VAPID_SUBJECT Web Push mailto:you@example.com or an https:// contact URL
PUSH_DISPATCH_SECRET Web Push ≥ 32 random characters; must equal the Vault secret diskarte_push_secret
GIPHY_API_KEY GIF picker Without it the GIF button says search isn't set up
SIGNUP_MODE Closing registration invite pauses public sign-up (also turn off "Allow new users to sign up" in Supabase so OAuth can't create accounts)
ALLOWED_ORIGINS Cross-origin API callers Comma-separated extra origins for CORS + CSRF on /api/*
RELEASE_ANNOUNCEMENTS Official update posts on lets each new production deployment post its release notes to Diskarte HQ #announcements (needs SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and the 20261107000000 migration). Set it for Production only

Push is enabled only when all five push values are valid (pushConfig() in lib/push-server.ts) and the database setup has run. Generate the keys once and keep them stable:

Terminal
cd diskarte
node -e 'console.log(require("web-push").generateVAPIDKeys())'
node -e 'console.log(require("node:crypto").randomBytes(32).toString("base64url"))'

Tuning#

Variable Default Description
RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_PER_MINUTE 5 Auth form POSTs per client IP per minute
RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_CALLBACK_PER_MINUTE 20 /auth/callback + /auth/confirm per IP per minute
RATE_LIMIT_API_PER_MINUTE 120 /api/* requests per IP per minute
APP_VERSION RENDER_GIT_COMMIT (first 7 chars), else dev Reported by /api/health
NODE_OPTIONS --max-old-space-size=384 in render.yaml Keeps Node inside a 512 MB free instance

Platform-provided#

Variable Set by Used for
PORT, HOSTNAME Dockerfile (3000, 0.0.0.0), Render injects PORT Standalone server bind address
NODE_ENV Next.js Dev-only CSP relaxations (unsafe-eval, localhost sockets)
RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL, RENDER_GIT_COMMIT Render SITE_URL fallback, health version
VERCEL_ENV Vercel Release announcements run only when it is production (or unset, e.g. Docker)
NEXT_RUNTIME Next.js instrumentation.ts only announces releases in the Node.js runtime
DISKARTE_SHARP_TARGET Dockerfile build stage (linuxmusl) Excludes non-musl sharp binaries from the standalone trace
NEXT_PUBLIC_IMAGE_HOSTS next.config.ts Internal: serialized image-optimizer host list for <SmartImage>

Testing#

Variable Used by Description
E2E_FULL Playwright 1 runs journeys that need Supabase + LiveKit (CI sets it)
E2E_BASE_URL Playwright Test an already-running deployment instead of starting the standalone build
E2E_PORT Playwright Port for the local standalone server (default 3000)
CI Playwright Retries, 2 workers, forbidOnly, GitHub reporter
DOCS_SCREENS npm run docs:screens 1 runs the screenshot specs that refresh the Help Center's product images

Supabase-side configuration (not environment variables)#

Setting Value
Auth → URL configuration Site URL = SITE_URL; redirect URLs include <SITE_URL>/auth/callback (and http://localhost:3000/auth/callback for dev)
Auth → Email Confirm email on; password minimum 10 with lowercase, uppercase, digits and symbols (matches the app's checklist)
Auth → OAuth providers Provider callback is https://<ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback
Realtime → Settings Allow public access: off
Vault diskarte_push_url, diskarte_push_secret (push only)

developers/testing.title: Testing
developers/testing.description: All commands run inside diskarte/ (or from the root with --prefix diskarte).
developers/testing.html:
Philosophy#

  • Test the rule where it lives. Authorization is in Postgres, so it is tested against the real migrations (in PGlite), as different users — not by mocking Supabase.
  • Fast and hermetic by default. npm test needs no Docker, network or credentials. Anything that needs live Supabase/LiveKit runs in CI's Playwright job.
  • Evidence, not certification. Browser suites use Chromium emulation; physical phones, Safari and real camera/microphone hardware are not covered automatically (see known limitations).

Test layers#

Layer Tooling Location Runs
Unit (pure logic) Vitest src/**/__tests__, tests/{security,deploy,community,…} npm test
Component / hook Vitest + Testing Library + jsdom src/components/**/__tests__, tests/ui, tests/workspace, tests/components npm test
Route handlers Vitest, handlers imported directly src/app/api/**/__tests__, tests/security/*-routes.test.ts npm test
Database / RLS Vitest + PGlite (Postgres compiled to WASM) tests/db/*.test.ts (one file per feature) npm test
Accessibility (components) axe-core in jsdom tests/a11y/axe.test.tsx npm test
Performance (virtualization) Vitest tests/performance/virtualization.test.tsx npm test
Documentation Vitest tests/docs/docs.test.ts, tests/docs/search.test.ts npm test
Responsive component browser Playwright + Vite, real components with fixture data tests/browser/experience.spec.ts npm run test:experience
End to end Playwright against the production standalone build e2e/*.spec.ts npm run test:e2e

All commands run inside diskarte/ (or from the root with --prefix diskarte).

Commands#

Terminal
cd diskarte
npm test                          # everything Vitest: unit, component, route, PGlite RLS, docs (~160 files)
npx vitest run tests/db/messages  # one file or pattern
npm run test:watch                # watch mode
npm run lint                      # ESLint (Next.js + React Compiler rules)
npm run typecheck                 # next typegen + tsc --noEmit
npm run build                     # production build (also required before local E2E)
npm run test:experience           # responsive component browser suite (needs Chromium)
npm run test:e2e                  # Playwright; journeys skip unless E2E_FULL=1
npm run db:check                  # read-only check that a Supabase project has the expected objects
npm run docs:db                   # regenerate docs/reference/database.md

Install the browser once: npx playwright install chromium.

Database / RLS tests#

tests/db/harness.ts boots a fresh PGlite instance, applies supabase-shim.sql (minimal auth, storage, realtime schemas, the anon/authenticated/service_role roles, auth.uid()/auth.jwt() and Supabase's default privileges) and then every migration, unmodified, in order.

TypeScript
// @vitest-environment node
import { beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { asUser, createDb, failure, one, signUp, type Db } from "./harness";

let db: Db;
let owner: string;
let outsider: string;
let general: string;

beforeAll(async () => {
  db = await createDb();
  owner = await signUp(db, "owner@diskarte.ph", { username: "kapitan" });
  outsider = await signUp(db, "out@diskarte.ph", { username: "outsider" });
  await asUser(db, owner);
  const serverId = (await one<{ id: string }>(db, "select public.create_server('Barkada', '') as id")).id;
  general = (await one<{ id: string }>(db, "select id from public.channels where server_id = $1 and type = 'text' order by position limit 1", [serverId])).id;
}, 60_000);

describe("scheduled messages", () => {
  it("refuses scheduling into a channel you can't see", async () => {
    await asUser(db, outsider);
    expect(await failure(db, "insert into public.scheduled_messages (channel_id, content, send_at) values ($1, 'hi', now() + interval '1 hour')", [general])).toBeTruthy();
  });
});

Helpers: signUp() inserts an auth.users row (firing the profile trigger), asUser() sets request.jwt.claim.sub and role authenticated, asAnon(), asService(), rows(), one() and failure() (returns the Postgres error message or null).

Things the shim does not emulate: PostgREST itself (pre-request hooks are called directly in tests), Realtime delivery, Storage object bytes, pg_cron, pg_net and Vault. Push installer SQL is exercised with stand-ins in tests/db/push-deployment.test.ts.

Gotchas:

  • Auto-mod drops repeated identical messages — give each test message distinct content.
  • Each test file creates its own database; keep fixtures inside the file.
  • To check a function's current definition after many migrations, query the catalog (pg_get_functiondef) rather than grepping migration files.

Component and hook tests#

tests/setup.ts registers global mocks so components render in jsdom:

Mock Replaces
mocks/livekit.ts livekit-client's Room and the LiveKit React hooks (tracks, speaking, participants driven by livekitMock)
mocks/navigation.ts next/navigation (router, params, pathname) and next/link
mocks/audio.ts AudioContext for the 8-bit sound effects
mocks/actions.ts Server Actions
fixtures/fake-supabase.ts A fake Supabase client with tables, RPCs and a Realtime emitter (order() is numeric-aware)
fixtures/server.tsx, fixtures/layout.tsx Ready-made server/member/channel contexts and a full signed-in layout
stubs/server-only.ts The server-only import guard (aliased in vitest.config.mts)

jsdom has a window, so it cannot catch SSR crashes from code touching window during render. tests/components/visit-beacon-ssr.test.tsx renders with renderToString for that reason; do the same for anything added to the root layout.

End-to-end tests#

playwright.config.ts starts npm run start:standalone (the last .next/standalone build — run npm run build first or you test stale code), uses Chromium with fake media devices, reduced motion, one worker locally (two in CI) and one retry in CI.

Spec Needs backend Covers
smoke.spec.ts no Landing, auth pages, CSP and security headers, 429 on auth brute force, API session gate, foreign-origin preflight
public-auth.spec.ts, landing-experience.spec.ts, appearance.spec.ts, pwa.spec.ts no Validation, navigation, reduced motion, themes, service worker caching and push dedupe
auth-profile.spec.ts yes Sign-up, onboarding, profile editing
server-chat.spec.ts yes Create a Tambayan, channels, two-user messaging
community.spec.ts yes Moderation, LFG, soundboard and community flows
events.spec.ts yes Event scheduling and RSVPs
sync-workspace.spec.ts yes Account sync and shared workspace conflicts
notifications.spec.ts yes Unreads, notification settings
layout.spec.ts, mobile.spec.ts yes Desktop columns/floating panels, phone navigation, 44 px tap targets, keyboard viewport
voice.spec.ts yes Two-person voice call with live preview
admin.spec.ts yes Control Center: non-admin refusal, sticky broadcast reaching another canvas, role change, ban
a11y.spec.ts yes axe-core audits of signed-in screens
docs.spec.ts no Help Center: home, navigation, search, copy buttons, diagrams, colour modes, 320–768 px layouts, internal pages not published, axe in dark and light

Journeys are skipped unless E2E_FULL=1. Locally that requires Docker for npx supabase start and a LiveKit dev server; without them, run the smoke specs:

Terminal
npm run build
set -a; source .env.local; set +a; unset RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_PER_MINUTE
SITE_URL=http://localhost:3997 E2E_PORT=3997 npx playwright test e2e/smoke.spec.ts

SITE_URL must match the port or the CSRF check returns 403; leaving a low auth rate limit makes the brute-force smoke test (which expects a 429) interact with other sign-in tests.

Continuous integration#

.github/workflows/ci.yml runs on pull requests, pushes to main and manual dispatch (feature-branch pushes alone don't trigger it):

The three jobs run in parallel. The Supabase CLI is pinned (supabase@2.122.1) so a new CLI major release can't break the E2E job; bump it deliberately and check supabase/config.toml still loads. On failure, the Playwright report and traces are uploaded as the playwright-report artifact for 7 days. No repository secrets are needed: CI uses a throwaway local Supabase stack and LiveKit's dev keys. Polling CI without the GitHub CLI: https://api.github.com/repos/xndrncp08/Diskarte/actions/runs.

Adding tests#

You changed… Add
A migration (table, policy, trigger, RPC) A tests/db/<feature>.test.ts case per role: outsider, member, the role just below the one allowed, the allowed role. Assert the error code, not just "fails"
A Server Action or route handler A unit test with the Supabase client mocked at the module boundary, covering auth, validation and each error mapping
A hook with realtime behaviour A test driving fake-supabase's emitter: duplicates, out-of-order events, reconnect
A component Testing Library by role/label; add it to tests/a11y/axe.test.tsx if it's a new surface
Something rendered in the root layout An SSR renderToString test
A user journey An e2e/*.spec.ts gated on FULL if it needs the backend

Known coverage gaps#

  • No automated tests on physical iOS/Android devices, Safari/WebKit or Firefox.
  • No load or soak testing; performance evidence is limited to virtualization tests and one-off bundle/LCP measurements in diskarte/docs/platform-experience.md.
  • Web Push is verified up to the browser's push event; delivery through Apple/Google/Mozilla push services is not.
  • pg_cron jobs are tested by calling their functions, not by the scheduler.
  • Production LiveKit webhooks and OAuth providers are not exercised in CI.

developers/design-system.title: UI, UX and design system
developers/design-system.description: Diskarte's look is Solar Gold on Midnight Navy glass with 8-bit touches: pixel status badges, arcade signal bars, stepped "arcade" easing and synthesized chiptune sound cues. The mascot is a character
developers/design-system.html:
Identity#

Diskarte's look is Solar Gold on Midnight Navy glass with 8-bit touches: pixel status badges, arcade signal bars, stepped "arcade" easing and synthesized chiptune sound cues. The mascot is a character in a salakot (the traditional wide-brimmed hat); default avatars are recoloured salakot mascots. Copy is English with Filipino flavour (status triggers like "Nagluto ng Canton", community names like Tambayan and Bantay-Bayan); core navigation and settings can be shown in Filipino.

Asset Source
Logo and wordmark Inline SVG React components (components/brand/); the wordmark uses glyph outlines from Knewave by Tyler Finck (SIL OFL 1.1, diskarte/assets/fonts/OFL-Knewave.txt)
App icons, favicons, OG images Rendered from the SVG components by npm run brand:assets
Landing hero Static mascot image with an optional WebGL "electric" logo, paused off-screen, disabled for reduced motion and low-power/mobile

The UI never draws emoji. Reactions, status icons, badges, sounds and activities are :code: strings rendered as vector icons by <Glyph> (lib/glyphs.ts), so they look the same on every platform.

Typography#

Token Font Use
--font-sans Inter Everything by default
--font-pixel Press Start 2P Retro headings and badges, sparingly
--font-silk Silkscreen Small pixel labels (role chips, counters)
--font-mono JetBrains Mono Code blocks and inline code

Fonts are self-hosted through next/font/google with display: swap. Phone inputs are 16 px so iOS doesn't zoom on focus.

Colour tokens#

Base palette in the Tailwind @theme block of globals.css:

Token Dark (default) Role
--color-sun / --color-sun-deep #ffb800 / #f59e0b Accent (the theme recolours this)
--color-midnight #0f172a Panels
--color-abyss #020617 Page background
--color-panel, --color-onyx #111827, #1e1f22 Raised surfaces

Diskarte Pulse#

Pulse is the redesign (Direction A, "Canvas": Spaces navigator, Conversation Canvas, Context sheet) in warm ink (dark) or paper (light) with a solar gold signature. It is built alongside Classic and reached per browser through the shell preference (ADR 016). This section covers the groundwork: tokens, fonts and the lint guard. The shared components (Button, Tabs, Sheet, Avatar…) and their contracts are in Pulse components. The app frame (Spaces navigator, canvas masthead, Context sheet, keyboard map, data sources) is in Pulse shell.

Scoping: Classic is untouched#

  • The diskarte-shell cookie (classic default, pulse) is read by the root layout, which renders <html data-shell="classic|pulse"> on the first byte (lib/shell.ts).
  • Every token lives in pulse.css under html[data-shell="pulse"], so Classic computes exactly the same styles as before. The Tailwind aliases (bg-pulse-surface…) are @theme inline, so they only resolve inside Pulse.
  • Pulse also repaints the page behind the app (html and body take --pulse-bg and --pulse-text, so overscroll, safe areas and the keyboard gap match), text selection (accent 35 %) and the focus outline (--pulse-focus-ring; Classic's sun outline is 1.6:1 on paper). High contrast keeps its own outline.
  • The only global additions are two breakpoints (see below) and the pulse-motion: variant (ambient motion only when neither the OS nor Settings asks for reduced motion); they add variants and change no existing ones.
  • setShell(shell, router) flips the attribute, saves the cookie and calls router.refresh(); no reload, so a live call, open chats and drafts survive the switch. Super admins switch it in Settings → Appearance ("Try the new Diskarte"); inside Pulse, Classic tokens map to Pulse ones (the Classic bridge, see Pulse shell) so reused Classic pages stay readable.

Lint guard#

Files in src/components/pulse/ may not use slate-*, gray-*, white or black colour utilities, Classic tokens (sun, sun-deep, midnight, abyss, onyx, panel, neon), arbitrary [#hex] colours, or hex colours in style props (no-restricted-syntax in eslint.config.mjs); the error points here. PulseSurface is the token-only reference and tests/ui/pulse-lint.test.ts proves the rule fires.

Reuse guidelines#

  1. Use components/ui primitives and semantic tokens; don't hard-code colours that themes or light mode should change.
  2. New overlays go through Modal/FloatingWindow/Popover so focus, Escape and stacking work.
  3. Heavy panels load lazily (next/dynamic or import()), with a skeleton.
  4. Check new UI in light mode, at 320 px width, with reduced motion and keyboard only.
  5. Never use emoji in UI chrome; add a glyph to lib/glyphs.ts instead.
