Contracts#

Each file's JSDoc header is the full contract; this is the summary.

Actions#

  • Button variant: primary (the one solar-gold action per view, on-accent text), secondary (outlined, default), quiet (text only), danger (on-alert text), live (joins or controls voice, on-live text). size: sm 32, md 40, lg 48 px; all are at least 44 px tall on coarse pointers (a real box, not a pseudo hit area). loading shows a spinner, disables and sets aria-busy. icon is a decorative leading icon. Pressing scales to 0.97 only under the pulse-motion variant.
  • IconButton label (required, becomes aria-label), icon, optional tooltip. Defaults to quiet. An empty label is reported with console.error outside production.

Labels and counts#

  • Chip a tag. Static; with onClick a toggle button (selected → aria-pressed); with onRemove a "Remove {name}" button. tone: neutral, accent, live, alert, people (tinted surface, coloured leading mark, text stays --pulse-text). Control radius, not a pill: circles are for people.
  • CountBadge count, label ("unread mentions"): screen readers hear "3 unread mentions", never a bare number. Shows max+ above max (99). tone: neutral (default, plain counts), alert (mentions), accent only where the count means "new" or "selected".
  • Kbd a key hint (<kbd>): <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>K</Kbd>; for a symbol pass label (<Kbd label="Enter">↵</Kbd>).
  • StatusBadge tinted pill with a mark or icon and the status as text.

Forms#

  • Input, Textarea, Select label (required), hint, error. Edges use --pulse-input-border (3:1); the error replaces the hint, turns the edge alert and is announced (role="alert", linked by aria-describedby). Select is native, so phones get their own picker.
  • Switch checked, onChange, label, hint, disabled. role="switch"; on is the accent-mark track, off an outlined track, and the knob position is the non-colour cue. On touch the 24 px track is a real 44 px box (transparent border). Disabled keeps readable text and greys the track.

Navigation#

  • Tabs label, items (id, label, badge?, disabled?), value, onChange, children (the active panel). APG tabs with automatic activation: one tab stop, ←/→ (wrapping), Home/End, disabled tabs skipped, aria-selected, aria-controls → role="tabpanel". The selected tab has a solar underline and bold text. The strip scrolls sideways on narrow screens.
  • NavItem a navigator row (Spaces, rooms, DMs): label, secondary?, leading? (Monogram, Avatar or icon; decorative), href (a link) or onClick (a button), current (aria-current="page", tint, bold label with a sun underline, never a side pill), unread (dot, bold, ", unread" for screen readers), count/countLabel/countTone, live (true or a label such as "3 in voice"), dimmed. 44 px tall.
  • BottomTabBar phone navigation: label, items (href, label, icon, current?, count?, countLabel?). A <nav> of links, not ARIA tabs; the current link has aria-current="page", bold text and a sun bar. Pads for the home indicator; position it yourself.
  • SegmentedControl label, options (value, label, icon?), value, onChange. A radio group: one tab stop, arrows move and select (wrapping), Home/End. The checked segment is raised, shadowed and bold.
  • Toolbar label, orientation?, children (IconButtons, Buttons). role="toolbar" with roving tabindex: one tab stop that remembers the last control, arrows move (wrapping), Home/End, disabled skipped.

Surfaces and overlays#

  • Card title?, action?, raised?. BentoGrid + BentoTile (title, eyebrow?, span: one, wide, tall, hero) for community pages; every tile is full width on phones.
  • Dialog open, onClose, title, description?, footer?. Centred card on the scrim, for a decision or a short form. First focus goes to the first [data-autofocus] element, else the first focusable one (Close). Put data-autofocus on the field when typing is the point: a type-to-confirm dialog (<Input label="Type the Space name to confirm" data-autofocus />) or a rename form. Don't put it on a destructive button.
  • Sheet same props. A side sheet from the right, or a bottom sheet (grabber, safe-area padding, keyboard-aware height) below 640 px. Use it for the Context sheet and other secondary panels.
  • Menu / ContextMenu the Classic props (label, items, trigger; useContextMenu, ContextMenuItems). Keyboard focus is the selected tint plus the global focus outline (high contrast relies on that outline). The first keyboard open focuses the first row (or the checked choice) as soon as the panel is positioned (useFloating reports ready). PulseMenuSkin gives every menu below it the Pulse skin; the Pulse shell root wraps its tree in it so reused Classic menus match.
  • Tooltip label, side. Visual only (aria-hidden); the trigger must name itself.

People and Spaces#

  • Avatar a person, always a circle: profile, size, status?, speaking?, labelled?. Decorative unless labelled (then the name and status are its accessible name).
  • Monogram a Space: a square tile with rounded-pulse-monogram (--pulse-radius-monogram, 7 px) and the initials or icon. Never a circle, and it never morphs on hover. selected adds the accent edge.
  • AvatarStack people (profiles with optional speaking), max (4), size, label?. Overlapping circles with "+N"; a speaker gets a live-teal ring with a gap. One role="img" named by the people shown ("Juan (speaking), Maria and 3 more").
  • PresenceDot status: online (disc), idle (crescent), dnd (barred disc), offline/invisible (ring), with the status name as the accessible name.

Signals and states#

  • PulseLine the sun "new since" separator; label names it (role="separator") and shows a pill. The travelling glint runs only under pulse-motion.
  • LiveIndicator teal dot, ripple (motion only) and the word "Live" (hideLabel keeps it for screen readers).
  • EmptyState title, body, icon? (in a neutral raised tile), action?, headingLevel?.
  • ErrorState what happened (title), what to do (body), and Try again (onRetry, retrying). role="alert".
  • Skeleton, SkeletonRows (message-shaped, announced once), Loading (neutral spinner and visible text, role="status").

Do and don't#

  • Do use one primary Button per view. Don't use gold for decoration; it means "the next step", "new" or "selected" (empty-state tiles, spinners and plain counts stay neutral).
  • Do pair every live, presence, mention or selected colour with a shape or words. Don't add a status that is only a colour.
  • Do put long context in a Sheet, a decision in a Dialog. Don't open one over the other.
  • Do use Avatar for people and Monogram for Spaces. Don't round a Space or square a person, and keep circles for people (chips and badges use the control radius).
  • Don't add floating hover toolbars or a server rail: Pulse is not Discord. Actions live in menus, context menus and the Context sheet.
  • Don't reach for Classic tokens, slate-*, white/black or hex colours in components/pulse; the lint guard fails the build.

Motion#

pulse-motion: (in pulse.css) applies only when the OS allows motion and Settings → Accessibility "Reduced motion" is off. Ambient loops (animate-pulse-travel, animate-pulse-ripple) and the press scale use it. Dialog and Sheet use framer-motion, which follows the app's MotionConfig (opacity only under reduced motion).

Visual review#

/pulse-gallery in the browser fixture (tests/browser/pulse-gallery.tsx, ?mode=light for paper) renders every component in every state. BentoGrid/BentoTile have no screen yet; they stay documented for community pages. tests/browser/pulse-gallery.spec.ts runs axe (WCAG 2.2 AA) in both modes at 390 and 1280 px with the page, the dialog, the sheet, the menu and a toast open, checks for horizontal overflow and the Tab order, and saves test-results/pulse-gallery-*.png. Unit tests are in tests/ui/pulse-components.test.tsx.

  • The bottom sheet does not support drag-to-dismiss yet (Escape, the scrim and Close all work).

developers/pulse-shell.html:
The application frame of Diskarte Pulse, direction "Canvas": a Spaces navigator on the left, the Conversation Canvas (a masthead over the page) and a Context sheet opened on demand. There is no server rail, no circle-to-squircle icon, no unread pill at the left edge and no user panel in the bottom-left corner. Built from the Pulse components; the decision is ADR 017.

Turning it on and off#

  • The diskarte-shell cookie picks the shell: pulse, or anything else (absent, classic, tampered) for Classic. Classic is the default and renders exactly as before.
  • Server gate (preview): the cookie counts only for super admins. previewShell(cookie, platformRole) (lib/shell.ts) is used by the tambayan layout and by the root layout's data-shell (which looks the role up only when the cookie asks for Pulse, and falls back to Classic on any error), so anyone else who sets the cookie by hand still gets Classic. The public opt-in comes in Step 7.
  • Super admins switch in Settings → Appearance → Try the new Diskarte (shown only for the server-provided super_admin role).
  • Pulse's "You" menu has Back to Classic.
  • Switching calls setShell (lib/shell.ts): it flips <html data-shell>, writes the cookie and runs router.refresh(). No reload, so a call stays connected.
  • Rollback: clear the cookie (or set it to classic). Nothing is stored server-side.

Architecture#

Text
app/(app)/layout.tsx           AdminAccessProvider (platform role) → SessionProviders (call, presence, social…)
└─ app/(app)/tambayan/layout   reads the cookie
   └─ ShellProviders           admin access, ShellKind, layout, unreads, ShellUI, watchers, ConfirmHost
      ├─ ClassicFrame          (Classic) rail + columns
      └─ PulseShell            (Pulse) PulseUI, PulseMenuSkin, PulseTooltipSkin
         ├─ Navigator          header, Home · People · Spaces, Jump to…, Pinned, the view
         └─ canvas column      BroadcastBanner, CallStrip, the page (WorkspacePanel "main")

Only the frame inside ShellProviders changes on a switch, so the call (in SessionProviders), unread counts and the membership, DM and reminder watchers stay mounted (tested in tests/ui/pulse-shell.test.tsx).

Pages were not rewritten. The components they already use read useShellKind() (ShellKind.tsx) and take a Pulse path:

WorkspacePanel id="main" <main id="main-content"> column The canvas: the same landmark on a Pulse surface card
ChannelHeader, PageHeader .page-header Masthead: the page's one h1 in Bricolage (display size from tablets up), the Space name, topic and member count, the page's actions (a Pulse search field), the Context toggle. The channel welcome under it shrinks to a small heading
ChatView's Pinned messages button Pins drawer Opens Context on the Pinned tab
RosterDrawer Member column ContextPanel: a Sheet, or a column when pinned at ≥ 1200 px
MemberList Everyone, offline dimmed 100 rows at a time with "Show more", offline at full contrast
[serverId]/layout.tsx — Renders <PulseRooms>, portalled into the navigator under the open Space
Classic tooltips and menus Classic look Pulse look (PulseTooltipSkin, PulseMenuSkin)

Shared logic was lifted out of Classic components rather than copied: useServerControls and useChannelMenuItems (ChannelSidebar), useStatusMenu (UserPanel), useGoAnywhere (WorkspaceControls), useServerBadge, useServerHref, the saved Space order (ServerRail), usePinnedMessages (PinsDrawer), useNavDrawer (the phone drawer's focus and Escape handling).

The Classic bridge#

Pages inside the canvas keep their Classic markup until Step 5. They read Classic tokens (--color-midnight, --color-white, --color-slate-*…); inside Pulse, pulse.css maps those to Pulse tokens so the text stays readable on Pulse surfaces in both modes. Accent tokens are untouched (the themes own them).

Navigator#

  • Header: "Diskarte", the notification hub and You (avatar with presence): status choices, Settings, the Control Center (super admins only) and Back to Classic.
  • Home · People · Spaces (SegmentedControl). The route picks the view (a DM or Friends shows People, a Space shows Spaces, the rest Home); a choice sticks until the next navigation.
  • Jump to… opens the Go anywhere palette (⌘/Ctrl K).
  • Pinned: Spaces and conversations pinned from their right-click menu.
  • Home: Home, Friends (request count), Messages (unread count), Explore, Search, Control Center.
  • People: Start a Hangout, a new group DM, Friends, then every conversation (hangout timers, unread dots).
  • Spaces: Diskarte HQ, then your Spaces in the order saved on the Classic rail, each a Monogram with mention count, unread dot, "In call" while you're in its voice room and the Classic server menu (plus Pin) on right-click. The open Space's row gets a "…" button (Classic's server menu: invite, settings, Bantay-Bayan, notifications, create channel, leave) and Invite, and the Space expands to its rooms as plain rows (no tree lines, no # icons): Overview (the Space's landing page), LFG Board, Shared workspace, Live (voice rooms with people in them, "N in voice"), then the rest. The default "Text Channels"/"Voice Channels" labels are hidden; custom categories keep theirs. Each room shows unread and mentions and has the Classic channel menu (copy link, mute, edit, delete).
  • The navigator is ≥ 280 px, resizable with the same saved width as Classic's channel column. On phones it is a full-height drawer (the menu button in the masthead, swipe, scrim, Escape or Back to close) that opens with focus on the current room or page.

Canvas and Context#

  • CallStrip: while you're in a call, a slim live strip across the top of the canvas (tablet and up): the room, connection meter, mute, deafen, mixer and disconnect. On phones it sits above the tab bar (Pulse on phones).
  • Masthead: see the seams table. The Context toggle is on channel pages.
  • Context sheet: People (the member list), Pinned (the channel's pinned messages, same query as the Pins drawer, fetched while the tab shows) and About (channel topic, Space description, rules). "Keep open beside the conversation" (≥ 1200 px) pins it as a column, remembered per browser (diskarte:pulse:context-pinned); in the column, Unpin turns it back into the open sheet and Close puts it away. The Pinned tab is keyed by channel, so another channel's pins never show while loading.

Data sources and privacy#

  • Spaces: servers from getMyServers (the tambayan layout); RLS returns only Spaces you belong to.
  • Rooms, members and voice occupancy: useServer(), the bundle [serverId]/layout.tsx loaded after its notFound() membership guard. Private rooms appear only when RLS returned them; occupancy is counted only for those rooms, so someone in a room you can't see never shows.
  • Conversations and friends: useSocial().
  • Pinned messages: a messages select, RLS-scoped like every message read.
  • The Control Center entry depends only on the server-provided platform role (AdminAccessProvider); the page re-checks it.
  • No use cache or unstable_cache; nothing is fetched client-side that the Classic UI doesn't already fetch.
  • Pins are saved in the display preferences (pins: ["space:<id>", "dm:<id>"], at most 20, validated on read), which sync through account_state under prefs:display and fall back to this browser when that table is missing. A pin to something you no longer belong to is never shown. The field is absent until you pin something, so Classic preferences keep their shape.

Keyboard#

Keys Where Does
⌘/Ctrl K Anywhere Jump to… (Go anywhere)
⌘/Ctrl ⇧ H, ⌘/Ctrl ⇧ M Anywhere Home, Messages
Alt (Option) 1–9 Anywhere but a text field, no dialog open Open the 1st–9th Space (HQ first, then your order) on its last room. Not ⌘/Ctrl: browsers keep those for tabs. Matched on the key position (Digit1…), since Option + digit types a symbol on macOS. Listed in Settings → Keybinds for super admins
↑ / ↓, Home / End Navigator lists Move between rows and their buttons (rooms included)
Escape Navigator Back to the canvas (#main-content); on phones it closes the drawer
← / → Home · People · Spaces, Context tabs Move and select
Shift F10, right-click, long-press Spaces, rooms, conversations Their menus

The skip link ("Skip to content") is the first Tab stop and lands on the canvas, which then shows a focus outline (keyboard focus only, in both shells). Tooltips open on hover and keyboard focus, not when a tap focuses a button.

Tests#

  • tests/ui/pulse-shell.test.tsx: a shell switch keeps the call and ShellProviders mounted, WorkspacePanel's two paths, RLS-scoped navigator data (no hidden rooms or their occupants, Control Center only for super admins), Alt 1–9 (and not Ctrl/⌘ or while typing), arrows and Escape, the Context tabs, openContext("pinned"), the You menu rejoining presence after Invisible, and pin storage. tests/ui/pulse-gate.test.tsx: only super admins get Pulse from the cookie.
  • tests/browser/pulse-shell.spec.ts: axe (WCAG 2.2 AA) in dark and light at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440 px on six routes, the phone navigator and the Context sheet; no horizontal overflow; an h1 in #main-content; the skip link; the pinned Context column. Screenshots: test-results/pulse-shell-*.png.
Terminal
cd diskarte && CI=1 npx playwright test --config playwright.experience.config.ts pulse-shell

Not yet#

  • Messages, the composer, DMs, threads and forums have their Pulse look: see Pulse messaging.
  • Messages, Friends, Shared workspace, Search, the Control Center, Home, Explore, the Space landing and the DM page use the Masthead: see Pulse communities and pages. Other page bodies (Moments, the Workspace body, the Control Center body) keep their Classic look in the canvas.
  • No Media tab in the Context sheet: recent attachments need a new query (Step 5).
  • Phones have their own tabs, screens and Back: see Pulse on phones. The voice redesign is Step 6a (the CallStrip is the Classic dock, re-laid-out).
  • Rooms can't be dragged to reorder in Pulse yet (moderators use Classic, or edit the channel).
  • Space-level live indicators only show your own call; other Spaces' voice activity needs the voice preview data per Space.

developers/pulse-messaging.title: Pulse messaging
developers/pulse-messaging.description: How messages, the composer, DMs, forums and threads look and behave inside the Pulse shell (direction "Canvas"). Classic renders exactly as before: every piece below is a useShellKind() === "pulse" br
developers/pulse-messaging.html:
How messages, the composer, DMs, forums and threads look and behave inside the Pulse shell (direction "Canvas"). Classic renders exactly as before: every piece below is a useShellKind() === "pulse" branch inside the existing component, sharing all data, hooks and actions.

Component Pulse path
MessageItem Margin transcript row, inline action row, long-press Sheet
ChatView, DmView Day dates, the New line, roving focus; DmView also uses the Masthead
ThreadPanel Pulse header and surface, same transcript and dock
ForumView Pulse search field, chips, votes and post cards; statuses in words
Composer The compose dock
ReactionBar, EditedMark Compact chips, "Edited" label
Transcript.tsx DaySeparator, UnreadLine, useReadPosition
useMessageRoving The log's keyboard model

Transcript#

  • Margin: each row is a two-column grid: a right-aligned margin (6.5rem from tablets up, 4.5rem on phones, where long names wrap to two lines) with the author's name and time, and the content column (capped at 72ch). No avatar: the name is the anchor. A message within 7 minutes of the same author's previous one (isGroupedWithPrevious) shares the margin: no repeated name, the time appears on hover or focus. Header rows get more space above them (12 px on phones, 16 px from tablets up) so a group reads as one block. The New line breaks a group (sharesMargin).
  • Accessible name: "Name (mentions you), 3:42 PM: preview", with the preview as plain text (previewText, 140 characters; "Sticker" or "Attachment" when there's no text), never raw markdown.
  • Text: Figtree at pulse-body with a 1.55 line height. Links in accent ink, code on --pulse-code in the mono font (paper mode swaps the highlight colours for darker ones that reach 4.5:1).
  • Labels: Edited and Pinned are small outlined caption labels, in words. Webhook and Official posts get a label in the margin.
  • Mentions of you: the mention tint plus a 3 px alert edge (shape) and "(mentions you)" in the row's accessible name, never colour alone.
  • Day separators: a quiet editorial date (Bricolage, muted) with a hairline.
  • New line: the sun PulseLine labelled "New · 3:42 PM" above the first message someone else sent after your read position (firstUnreadIndex). useReadPosition snapshots the read position when the conversation opens (or when the unread counts first arrive) and keeps the line in place while you read; it only moves back (Mark Unread). Nothing unread on open, no line. Channels read UnreadsProvider's readAt; Pulse waits for those counts before marking the channel read, so a fresh load still knows. DMs read SocialProvider's lastReadAt.
  • Reply quote: a "ticket stub": a raised tab with a dashed top edge, the author's name and a preview; it jumps to the original.
  • Reactions: compact chips (icon and count). Yours: accent tint, accent edge and bold count. The press scale runs only under pulse-motion.
  • Attachments, link previews, voice notes: .chat-card raised cards on the line token.
  • Receipts (DMs): "Sent" / "Seen" as a caption under your last message.

Actions#

  • No floating toolbar. An inline action row under the content: Reply, React (the emoji picker), Thread (channels) and More… (the message's context menu, the same MessageMenuItems as right-click, opened with useContextMenu().openFrom). It is a Pulse Toolbar (one Tab stop, arrow keys).
  • When it shows (pulse.css): on keyboard focus; while one of its popups is open; and once opened (data-actions="open", by Enter or the margin button) until focus moves to another message or leaves the log. Never on hover alone: the row takes space, and revealing it under the pointer would push the log around.
  • Pointer: hovering a message shows one quiet Message actions button (…, 24 px) at the left edge of its margin (tablets up; the margin reserves room for it). Clicking it opens the row and focuses Reply. It is tabIndex=-1: keyboard users reach the row with Enter.
  • Touch: long-press (the existing useContextMenu gesture) opens the actions in a bottom Sheet instead of a floating menu; swipe to reply is unchanged.

Keyboard#

Keys Where Does
Tab Into the log Lands on the last focused message, else the newest. The log is one Tab stop
↑ / ↓, Home / End A message Previous / next message, first / last loaded (scrolls a virtualized row in first)
Enter or → A message Into its action row (Reply first)
← / → Action row Between actions
Escape Action row Back to the message
Tab / Shift+Tab A message Leaves the log
Shift F10, Menu key A message Its context menu

Enter lands on Reply, so Enter twice replies to the message. Inside the row, Tab past the last action leaves the log, and Shift+Tab from the first action (Reply) goes back to the message, not to the previous message's controls. While focus is anywhere in the log its live region is switched off (aria-live="off"), so new messages aren't read out over the one you're on; it goes back to polite when focus leaves. The typing line above the dock is not a live region either: it changes too often to announce.

VirtualMessageList takes the roving handlers through its roving prop; the scroller itself becomes focusable only while the tab-stop message is scrolled out of the DOM, and hands focus to it. Rows stay plain DOM (no framer-motion).

Compose dock#

  • A raised card (rounded-pulse-card, shadow-pulse-2) a little above the bottom edge: the field on top (16 px on phones so iOS doesn't zoom, pulse-body from tablets up), the tools underneath (Attach, Voice note, GIF, Emoji, Sticker, Poll, Schedule, each where it existed before; the GIF, emoji and sticker pickers take a Pulse triggerClassName), slow mode and the character count, then Send as the sun pill with an Enter key hint (Kbd, hidden on phones).
  • Above the dock: the typing line (words first; the dots only move under pulse-motion) and the reply ticket stub with Cancel reply.
  • Everything else is the Classic composer's logic, unchanged: drafts and their sync notice, slash commands (Tab to complete), mention requests, uploads and their gates (uploads={false} in Hangouts), drag and drop, paste, slow mode, locks (a Pulse notice card), the offline queue, scheduling, Enter / Shift+Enter, ↑ to edit your last message, Escape to cancel a reply. The keyboard-safe height comes from the shell's useAppViewport, as in Classic.

DMs, threads and forums#

  • DMs: the Masthead (name, "Direct message" / "Group" / "Hangout", calls, Leave group), the transcript with the New line and receipts, the dock.
  • Threads: a Pulse surface with a header ("Thread in #room", the root's preview, Close), the root message, the replies with roving focus, the dock.
  • Forums: the search field, filter chips, votes and post cards on Pulse tokens; a post's status is a word on an outlined chip with a coloured mark.

Tests#

  • tests/ui/pulse-messaging.test.tsx: grouping and the New line (firstUnreadIndex, sharesMargin, useReadPosition), the roving keyboard model (logIndex, Tab in and out, Enter, Escape), the action row's names and tab stop, More… opening the message menu, mentions and the reply stub in words, Classic unchanged, and the dock keeping Enter / Shift+Enter / ↑ / Escape, the tools, slow mode, the upload gate and the lock notice.
  • tests/browser/pulse-messaging.spec.ts: axe (WCAG 2.2 AA) in dark and light at 390 and 1280 px on the channel, DM, forum and thread, no horizontal overflow, the keyboard path through the log, and screenshots in test-results/pulse-messaging-*.png. Fixtures: tests/browser/pulse-messaging-data.ts.
Terminal
cd diskarte && CI=1 npx playwright test --config playwright.experience.config.ts pulse-messaging

Not yet#

  • The pickers' panels (GIF, sticker, emoji, poll, schedule) keep their Classic look, readable through the Classic bridge; the voice, poll and schedule triggers too.
  • No avatars in the margin; a per-user preference could add small ones later.
  • Forum post bodies open in the thread panel as before; the forum has no Pulse empty-state illustration.

developers/pulse-communities.description: Step 5b of Diskarte Pulse: a Space's landing page, Explore, Home, the Messages inbox and the page headers. Built from the Pulse components inside the Pulse shell. Pulse is a super-admin preview (the s
developers/pulse-communities.html:
Step 5b of Diskarte Pulse: a Space's landing page, Explore, Home, the Messages inbox and the page headers. Built from the Pulse components inside the Pulse shell. Pulse is a super-admin preview (the server gate in previewShell); Classic renders exactly as before. Every page shares its data and logic with Classic and takes its Pulse path through useShellKind().

Community landing (/tambayan/[serverId])#

Classic still redirects the Space's index to its first text room. In Pulse the index page (after the layout's notFound() membership guard) renders CommunityLanding. A link with ?event=<id> still goes to the first room, where the event opens. The navigator's Space row keeps opening the last room; the new Overview row at the top of the Space's rooms opens the landing.

  • Header: the Masthead (the Space name as the h1, member and online counts), then a cover-style hero: the banner or a plain accent band (decorative, no text), the icon overlapping it, the description, the category and Open #room (the page's one primary action, full width on phones).
  • Bento tiles: Rooms (six at most: live voice rooms, then rooms with unread or mentions, then the rest; the navigator's rows and right-click menus; All N rooms opens the navigator drawer on phones and moves focus to the Space's rooms on desktop. Private rooms' occupancy is on their own topic, so they rank as quiet here), Coming up (the next three events, relative times), Start here (welcome message, rules, a link to the welcome room), People (faces, online count, custom roles, See everyone opens the Context sheet), Shared workspace, Boards (LFG, forums and suggestion boards), Invite (not in Diskarte HQ) and, for moderators with approval on, Join requests (opens Server settings → Membership).
  • Who sees what: landingTiles() (lib/community-identity.ts) gates tiles by role. Rooms, members and roles come from useServer() (the RLS-scoped bundle), events from a server_events select on the page (RLS-scoped), the join-request count from useJoinRequestCount(), which only queries (and only listens for focus) for moderators of a Space with approval on. No use cache.

Banner and accent#

The banner_url and accent_color columns come from migration 20261109010000 (branch feat/community-identity, not merged yet). They are optional in database.types.ts and read as server.banner_url ?? null, so the landing and Explore work with or without the migration (no banner, no accent).

  • Banner allow-list: communityBanner(url, supabaseUrl) returns the URL only when it is a public object in this project's avatars bucket (<SUPABASE_URL>/storage/v1/object/public/avatars/…, same scheme and host, no credentials, a path of plain characters only: no .., %2e, %2f, %5c or any other percent-encoding, so no encoded or double-encoded variant can leave the bucket). Anything else is ignored, because an arbitrary https host could log who views the page. The image is decorative (alt="", referrerPolicy="no-referrer").
  • Accent on-colour: communityAccent(hex) returns the accent with whichever of white and #121016 contrasts more (the migration's check constraint guarantees one reaches 4.5:1). Nothing puts text on the accent today (the band and Explore's stripe are decorative); the on-colour is for the coming picker. Malformed values are ignored.
  • No banner upload UI yet; it belongs in Server settings next to the icon (uploadPublicImage(…, "banner", …) → servers/<id>/banner-<uuid>.(jpg|png|webp)), admin-only, once the migration ships.

Explore (/tambayan/explore)#

PulseExplore: Masthead, an editorial "Find your tambayan" headline (tablets and up; phones go straight to search), the search field, the categories on their own row as single-select toggle chips (aria-pressed) that wrap so none is cut off, then communities as cards (the first one featured two columns wide when there are three or more), each with its banner or accent stripe when set. ExploreView keeps the discover_servers query, paging, retry and the join flow, membership screening dialog included, so both shells behave the same. Non-members see only what discover_servers returns.

Home (/tambayan)#

PulseHome gets everything HomeView already computes and lays it out as "Where should I go next?" (the first h2, above the fold on phones): tiles for conversations, mentions and friend requests, friends around with Start a Hangout (the page's one primary action), live voice rooms (the same voice preview), events, your Spaces (to their landings) and create / join / add friends. Getting started (the shared component, restyled by [data-pulse-home] rules in pulse.css) sits above the tiles only for new accounts, otherwise after them with What's new and Moments. Times are relative ("5 min. ago", "in 2 days", via RelativeTime). Same dialogs as Classic, no feed.

Messages: a focused inbox#

The navigator's People view already lists every conversation, so in Pulse /tambayan/messages is an inbox (PulseInbox) rather than a second copy: the Masthead with the unread count, a search field, All / Unread (n), and roomier rows (avatar, name, when it last moved, hangout timer, unread dot). Conversations carry no last-message text, so rows show when they last moved (relative) rather than a preview; a preview needs a new query. Friends and new group DMs stay in the navigator. The filtering is MessagesView's, unchanged.

Page headers#

Friends, Shared workspace, Search and the Control Center render the Masthead in Pulse (eyebrow, display-size title, icon, description; the phone navigator button comes with it). Their Classic headers are untouched.

  • Friends: the tabs take the Pulse look (tint plus sun underline when selected, accent count on Pending, Add Friend as the gold action until chosen); same tablist and keys.
  • Control Center: AdminControlCenter pulse renders the Masthead itself, with Live/Polling (a StatusBadge) and Refresh (an IconButton, 44 px on touch) as its actions and "Updated …" as the description, instead of its own icon and h2.

Tests#

  • tests/ui/pulse-communities.test.tsx: accent on-colour (higher contrast wins, at the crossover), the banner allow-list (other hosts, look-alike hosts, other buckets, .., %2e, %2f, %5c, double encoding, http), tile gating by role, only moderators querying join requests, the six-room Rooms tile with All rooms, relative times, the banner rendered only from the bucket, and the landing without the identity columns.
  • tests/browser/pulse-communities.spec.ts: the landing, Explore, Home, Messages and Friends in dark and light at 390 and 1280 px: axe (WCAG 2.2 AA) with no violations, no horizontal overflow, the Masthead h1; the inbox filter and the Explore categories. Screenshots: test-results/pulse-communities-*.png.
Terminal
cd diskarte && CI=1 npx playwright test --config playwright.experience.config.ts pulse-communities

Not yet#

  • Banner upload and accent picker in Server settings (needs the migration).
  • A last-message preview in the inbox (needs the conversations query to return it).
  • Moments and the Friends, Workspace and Control Center bodies keep their Classic look under the bridge.

developers/pulse-mobile.title: Pulse on phones
developers/pulse-mobile.description: Step 6b of Diskarte Pulse: phone navigation that is designed for a phone rather than a shrunk desktop. It sits in the Pulse shell and is built from the Pulse components. Pulse is still a super-admin p
developers/pulse-mobile.html:
Step 6b of Diskarte Pulse: phone navigation that is designed for a phone rather than a shrunk desktop. It sits in the Pulse shell and is built from the Pulse components. Pulse is still a super-admin preview; Classic's phone layout (its MobileNavigation, colours and drawer) is unchanged.

"Phone" means below md (768 px). A phone in landscape (for example 844 × 390) is wider than that and gets the tablet layout: the navigator column, no tab bar.

Screens and tabs#

MobileTabs.tsx holds the route rules and the bottom area. The BottomTabBar (a <nav> of links labelled "Main destinations", not ARIA tabs) has four destinations:

Tab Route Also current on
Home /tambayan Search, Control Center
People /tambayan/messages (the Pulse inbox) Friends
Spaces /tambayan/spaces (new) Explore, a Space's landing (/tambayan/[serverId])
You /tambayan/you (new) —
  • phoneTab(pathname) says which tab a screen belongs to, or null for a conversation: a DM, a room, or a Space's inner pages (workspace, LFG board). Conversations get the whole screen and no tab bar, so the keyboard has room.
  • People is the inbox plus, on phones, a Friends row at the top (with the request count) and Start a Hangout / Group pinned at the bottom in thumb reach (PeopleActions, shared with the navigator's People view).
  • Spaces (views/Spaces.tsx) lists your Spaces in the saved order (useSpaces, SpaceRow, the navigator's rows). A tap opens the Space's landing, where its rooms are; long-press opens the Space menu. Explore Spaces, then Add a Space at the bottom.
  • You (views/You.tsx) shows your face and status, the status and custom status choices (useStatusMenu, pressed toggles under an h2 per group), Notification settings, then Settings, the Control Center (super admins) and Back to Classic (useYouItems, shared with the You menu). The notification hub is in its masthead.
  • The two new routes need no new data: Spaces reads getMyServers like Messages; You reads the profile already in MeProvider. Both check previewShell on the server and send Classic to /tambayan. Every route still opens directly (deep links).
  • The phone navigator drawer stays: the masthead's menu button on top-level screens, a swipe from the left edge, and a landing's "All N rooms". Its Home · People · Spaces switch is unchanged.

Conversations, Back and gestures#

  • The Masthead shows Back instead of the menu button in a conversation. backTarget(pathname): a DM goes to People, anything inside a Space to its landing. useBack() returns through history when you came from that screen (so the list keeps its scroll) and otherwise pushes it (a deep link has no history to go back to).
  • A swipe from the left edge goes Back in a conversation (the same useSwipeDrawer gesture that opens the drawer on top-level screens).
  • A conversation opened from a top-level screen slides in from the right: the canvas gets data-enter and max-md:pulse-motion:data-enter:animate-pulse-enter (260 ms, no fill mode, so no transform lingers). Under reduced motion (OS or Settings) it simply appears.
  • Focus: after a navigation on a phone, focus moves to the new screen's h1 (made focusable with tabIndex=-1), else the canvas, so screen readers start on the new screen. Desktop keeps focus where it was.

Sheets#

  • Long-press on a Space, room or conversation opens its menu in a bottom Sheet on touch screens (pointer: coarse). The shared ContextMenu reads TouchMenuContext; PulseMenuSkin provides a Sheet, Classic provides nothing and keeps its floating menu. The click that follows lifting the finger is dropped, so it can't close the sheet or pick a row. Messages already did this (Step 5a).
  • The Context panel is a bottom Sheet on phones. Sheets close with Escape, the scrim, Close or Back.

Calls, keyboard and safe areas#

  • During a call the live CallStrip sits above the tab bar, and at the bottom of a conversation. Until the voice step's compact variant lands, the default strip is un-hidden on phones (marked shortcut: in the code).
  • Keyboard: useKeyboardUp() follows useAppViewport's <html data-keyboard>; while the keyboard is up the tab bar and call strip are not rendered and the composer or search field stays in view. Inputs are 16 px on phones (no iOS zoom).
  • Safe areas: the shell pads for the status bar (phones) and, in Pulse at every width, the left and right insets (landscape notch). The tab bar pads for the home indicator; with no tab bar, a spacer does. The shell is plain h-dvh with no measured heights outside the keyboard, so an installed app (standalone) has no bottom gap.
  • Touch targets are real 44 px boxes: the tab bar, masthead buttons, rows, and the SegmentedControl's segments (now at least 44 px wide on touch). Pulse's Pinned messages button in a room is a Pulse IconButton.

Tests#

  • tests/ui/pulse-mobile.test.tsx: the tab and Back rules, the four tabs with the current one and the unread count, no tabs in a conversation, Back by history and by deep link, the edge swipe (Back in a conversation, the drawer elsewhere), focus on the new h1 and the slide attribute, the keyboard hiding the tabs, the call strip above the tabs, the Spaces and You screens, and context menus as a sheet on touch (floating with a mouse).
  • tests/browser/pulse-mobile.spec.ts (Chromium with touch emulation, not real devices): seven screens at 320 × 640, 375 × 812, 390 × 844, 430 × 932 and 844 × 390 in dark and light: tabs only on top-level screens, axe (WCAG 2.2 AA) with no violations, no horizontal overflow, and a 44 px probe of the masthead, tab bar and the People, Spaces and You pages. Flows: tabs, a DM and Back, Spaces to a landing, a room and an edge swipe back, a deep link's Back; the long-press Space sheet and the Context sheet with Escape; safe-area insets emulated through CDP (Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride, skipped when the Chromium build lacks it). Screenshots: test-results/pulse-mobile-*.png.
Terminal
cd diskarte && CI=1 npx playwright test --config playwright.experience.config.ts pulse-mobile

Not yet#

  • Real-device checks (iOS Safari, Android Chrome, installed PWA): everything above is browser emulation.
  • Swipe-to-dismiss on sheets, and an interactive (finger-following) Back swipe; the swipe triggers after 56 px.
  • The compact call strip (voice step) and the voice room's phone layout.
  • Room and DM pages inside a conversation have no quick switcher besides Back; the drawer is one tap away from the landing.

developers/decisions.html:
Short records of decisions that shape the codebase. Each was reconstructed from the code, migration comments and release notes; the date is when the decision shows up in history. New decisions use the ADR template and are appended here.

# Decision Status
001 Authorization lives in Postgres (RLS, triggers, definer RPCs) Accepted
002 Runtime configuration; one image for every environment Accepted
003 Private Realtime channels only Accepted
004 Client-generated message ids for idempotent sends Accepted
005 The LiveKit call lives in the persistent app layout Accepted
006 Self-contained app folder, not an npm workspace Accepted
007 Hosted-only jobs are installed outside migrations Accepted
008 Database outbox for Web Push Accepted
009 Additive, forward-only migrations applied by hand Accepted
010 Free-tier first Accepted
011 Vercel for production, Docker kept portable Accepted
012 Vector glyph vocabulary instead of emoji Accepted
013 Help Center rendered at authoring time inside the app Accepted
014 Release announcements published by the deployment itself Accepted
015 Hangouts are temporary group conversations Accepted
016 Pulse ships behind a per-browser shell preference Accepted
017 One frame mount, shell-aware seams Accepted

001. Authorization lives in Postgres#

Context. The browser talks to Supabase directly (PostgREST, Realtime, Storage) for most reads and many writes; Server Actions are only one of several paths. Decision. Every table has RLS; field-level rules (who may change a role, pin, edit, move a channel between servers) are BEFORE triggers raising coded exceptions (ONLY_MODERATORS_CAN_PIN, SLOWMODE…); multi-step operations are SECURITY DEFINER functions with search_path = '' that re-check auth.uid(). anon has no table privileges. The app never uses the service role for user requests. Consequences. One rule set covers every path. UI permission helpers (e.g. canManageMember in lib/servers.ts) only mirror database rules to hide controls. New functions must explicitly revoke … from public, anon because Supabase's default privileges grant EXECUTE to authenticated and anon.

002. Runtime configuration, one image#

Decision. lib/env.ts reads process.env per request and validates it with Zod; the root layout passes public values to the client through RuntimeConfigProvider instead of NEXT_PUBLIC_* build-time inlining. Consequences. The same Docker image runs locally, in CI and in production. Missing configuration shows a ConfigNotice instead of crashing, and /api/health reports it.

003. Private Realtime channels only#

Context. On 2026-10-02 production had Realtime's "Allow public access" off and public Postgres Changes subscriptions silently delivered nothing. Decision. All channels are private; can_access_realtime_topic() authorizes every topic prefix; subscribeDbChanges() sets the socket's JWT before joining. Consequences. New topics need a migration. CI can't catch a public subscription (local Supabase allows them), so reviews must.

004. Client-generated message ids#

Decision. The composer generates the message UUID; retries reuse it; the server treats a unique violation as "already sent". Consequences. Idempotent offline queues without a dedupe table; Realtime echoes reconcile by id.

005. The call lives in the root app layout#

Decision. CallProvider is mounted by app/(app)/layout.tsx; settings open as a dialog. Consequences. Calls survive navigation. A full reload (including after a deploy) still drops the call, mitigated by the 30-second sessionStorage rejoin.

006. Self-contained app folder#

Context. Render (and Vercel) build with Root Directory diskarte and can't see files above it. Decision. The app has its own lockfile and Dockerfile; the root package.json only forwards scripts. The retired early-access portal was deleted rather than shared. Consequences. Nothing needed at build time may live outside diskarte/. Documentation and migrations may.

007. Hosted-only jobs outside migrations#

Decision. pg_cron, pg_net and Vault setup live in diskarte/docs/sql/*.sql, run once by the database owner. Consequences. Migrations run unmodified in PGlite and CI. Features degrade gracefully when the jobs aren't installed (see background-jobs.md).

008. Database outbox for push#

Decision. Triggers enqueue push work in the same transaction as the source row; an authenticated HTTP dispatcher drains it with leases. Consequences. No message is pushed for a rolled-back insert; access is rechecked at send time; delivery is at least once. Requires pg_net, Vault and a reachable dispatcher URL.

009. Additive, forward-only migrations#

Decision. Migrations add tables/columns/functions and replace functions; they don't drop user data. They are reviewed and applied by hand (SQL Editor or supabase db push), never by a deploy. Consequences. App rollbacks never require schema rollbacks — older code ignores new columns. New features must tolerate a database that hasn't been migrated yet (hide the feature, show a "couldn't" toast or an unavailable state).

010. Free-tier first#

Decision. Defaults fit Supabase/LiveKit/Render free tiers: in-memory rate limits (Upstash optional), lazy heavy SDKs, NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=384, a 150 MB image budget enforced in CI. Consequences. On multi-instance hosts (Vercel), set Upstash for shared auth rate limits; the link preview cache is per instance.

011. Vercel for production#

Context. 2026-10-12: Render's free tier sleeps and cold-starts slowly. Decision. Production runs on Vercel (diskarte-ten.vercel.app, functions next to the Supabase region). The Docker image and render.yaml stay supported; the proxy 308-redirects page requests on any host other than SITE_URL. Consequences. Vercel deploys main on push, in parallel with CI — watch CI and load a page after every push. Serverless instances don't share memory.

012. No-emoji glyph vocabulary#

Decision. Reactions, statuses, badges and activities are :code: strings rendered as vector icons by <Glyph> (lib/glyphs.ts); the database validates reaction codes. Consequences. Consistent rendering across platforms; custom server emoji use the same :name: syntax backed by images.

013. Help Center rendered at authoring time inside the app#

Status. Accepted — 2026-11-06

Context. The Markdown docs live in the repository root, but hosts build only diskarte/. A public Help Center needed search, navigation and diagrams without new infrastructure or a heavier signed-in app. Decision. scripts/build-docs-site.mts renders the pages listed in docs/site.json to HTML and a search index, committed inside the app (like the generated database reference) and served at /docs by the existing Next.js app. Pages are Server Components that inject the pre-rendered HTML; only search, copy buttons, the table-of-contents highlight and Mermaid (lazy, only on pages with diagrams) run in the browser. Alternatives considered. Fumadocs/Nextra (a second app or MDX pipeline, a separate deploy and a styling system to reconcile); rendering Markdown per request (ships a parser and highlighter to the server for every view); an external search service (cost, and private pages could leak into it). Consequences. No new deployment; the docs inherit the app's themes, CSP and fonts. Authors run npm run docs:site after editing published Markdown (the docs test fails otherwise). Publication is an explicit allow-list, so new runbooks stay off the site by default.

014. Release announcements published by the deployment itself#

Status. Accepted — 2026-11-07

Context. Each meaningful release should be announced in Diskarte HQ, but only once it is actually live: not on push, not for failed or preview builds. There is no GitHub CLI or repository secret available to wire a CI step, and pushes to main deploy on Vercel in parallel with CI. Decision. A production server instance announces its own release from instrumentation.ts register() (opt-in RELEASE_ANNOUNCEMENTS=on, production only). Notes are developer-written JSON formatted deterministically. A service-role-only SQL function posts once per release under an advisory lock and refuses older releases after newer ones. Alternatives considered. A GitHub Actions job on Vercel's deployment_status (needs a repository secret and an exposed publish endpoint); a Vercel deployment webhook (plan-dependent, another secret); publishing from CI on merge (would announce failed deployments). Consequences. Every instance start costs one cheap RPC (not awaited). If the first attempt fails, the next instance retries. Super admins can retry, withdraw or republish in the Control Center.

015. Hangouts are temporary group conversations#

Status. Accepted — 2026-11-08

Context. Friends needed a spontaneous way to talk and call without creating a permanent Tambayan, and without leaving abandoned rooms or files behind. Decision. A Hangout is a dm_conversations group row with an end time (hangout_until). It reuses group-DM text, read state, Realtime, the DM call room and rings unchanged. Expired hangouts stop accepting messages immediately (trigger) and are deleted by purge_expired_hangouts (platform job, and whenever a hangout is created). Uploads are refused while temporary so deletion never orphans Storage objects; "Keep" clears the end time. Alternatives considered. A new hangouts table with its own messages and LiveKit rooms (duplicates DMs, calls and their RLS); temporary Tambayans (channels, roles and invites are far more than a quick get-together needs, and cleanup would touch many tables). Consequences. Every DM code path already handles hangouts; the UI only adds the end-time bar, list badges and the start dialog. Hangouts follow group-DM rules (friends only, ≤ 10 people). Files need the hangout to be kept first.

016. Pulse ships behind a per-browser shell preference#

Status. Accepted — 2026-11-08

Context. The Diskarte Pulse redesign (Spaces navigator, Conversation Canvas, Context sheet) replaces the whole look. It has to be built and tested in production-like conditions over several releases while Classic, the current UI, stays exactly as it is for everyone else. Decision. A diskarte-shell cookie (classic by default, or pulse) is read by the root layout, which server-renders <html data-shell> like the theme and colour mode. Every Pulse style is scoped to html[data-shell="pulse"] (pulse.css) and Pulse components live in components/pulse/, lint-restricted to Pulse tokens. Switching sets the attribute, writes the cookie and calls router.refresh() (lib/shell.ts), never a full reload, so the call and session providers in the (app) layout stay mounted. Alternatives considered. A separate route tree or app (duplicates data loading and would drop the call when switching); a server-side flag per account (needs a migration and makes a stuck user unable to switch back in another browser); a localStorage flag (the server can't see it, so the first paint would flash the wrong shell). Consequences. Classic needs no changes and its tests prove it is untouched. Pulse fonts load only when Pulse styles use them. Until there is a visible switch, Pulse is reached by setting the cookie. The preference is per browser, like the theme; syncing it across devices would be a later decision.

017. One frame mount, shell-aware seams#

Status. Accepted — 2026-11-10

Context. The Pulse shell (Spaces navigator, canvas, Context sheet) has to wrap every existing page (Home, Explore, Search, Messages, Friends, DMs, channels, the Control Center) without duplicating their data loading, actions or permission checks, and switching shells must not drop a call or the unread state. Decision. app/(app)/tambayan/layout.tsx is the only place a frame is chosen: it reads the diskarte-shell cookie and renders <PulseShell> or <ClassicFrame> inside one shared <ShellProviders> (admin access, layout, unreads, shell toggles, watchers, confirm host), so a switch swaps only the frame. Pages stay as they are. The seams they already use read a ShellKindContext: WorkspacePanel (nav renders nothing in Pulse, main is the canvas), ChannelHeader and PageHeader (the masthead), RosterDrawer (the Context sheet) and MemberList (paged). The open Space's rooms are rendered by [serverId]/layout.tsx, after its membership guard and inside its ServerProvider, and portalled into a slot in the navigator. Classic content inside Pulse reads Classic tokens, which pulse.css maps to Pulse ones (the Classic bridge). Alternatives considered. A parallel (pulse) route tree (every page and loader twice); having each page branch on the shell (dozens of edits, easy to miss one); the navigator fetching the Space's rooms itself (a second, client-side data path beside the RLS-scoped server bundle). Consequences. Classic renders exactly as before and its tests are unchanged. Pulse inherits every page, action and permission check, and shows only data the server layouts already loaded. Pages keep their Classic look inside the canvas until Steps 5 and 6 restyle them. Rolling back is clearing the cookie.

developers/contributing.title: Contributing
developers/contributing.description: Thanks for helping build Diskarte. This guide covers how the repository is organized, how changes flow from a branch to production, and the conventions reviewers expect.
developers/contributing.html:
Thanks for helping build Diskarte. This guide covers how the repository is organized, how changes flow from a branch to production, and the conventions reviewers expect.

Repository organization#

Path What lives there Notes
diskarte/ The Next.js app — self-contained (own package-lock.json, Dockerfile) Hosts build with Root Directory diskarte; nothing it needs at build time may live outside it. Add dependencies from inside this folder
diskarte/src/app/ Routes (App Router): (auth), (app)/tambayan/*, (app)/settings, api/*, auth/* (app)/layout.tsx owns the session providers
diskarte/src/actions/ Server Actions, one file per domain Thin: validate, rate-limit, call Supabase as the user, translate errors
diskarte/src/components/<domain>/ UI by domain (chat, voice, server, shell, social, profile, admin, workspace, ui…) ui/ holds shared primitives
diskarte/src/hooks/ Client hooks for live data and gestures
diskarte/src/lib/ Pure logic, clients and schemas lib/schemas/ (Zod), lib/supabase/ (clients + generated types), lib/data/ (server reads)
diskarte/src/proxy.ts Request gate (Next.js 16's middleware)
diskarte/tests/, diskarte/e2e/ Vitest suites (incl. PGlite DB tests) and Playwright specs See Testing
diskarte/scripts/ grant-admin.mjs, check-database.mjs, brand asset generators, generate-db-reference.mts
diskarte/docs/ Feature runbooks and hosted-only SQL installers Linked from these docs
supabase/migrations/ The database schema Filename order = apply order
docs/ This documentation

The repository is not an npm workspace. From the root, npm install runs npm ci in the app and npm run <script> forwards to npm run <script> --prefix diskarte.

Before you write code#

This project uses Next.js 16, which changes APIs and conventions (for example proxy.ts instead of middleware.ts, PageProps<"/route"> / LayoutProps helpers generated by next typegen). Read the relevant guide in diskarte/node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before relying on memory, and heed deprecation notices.

Development workflow#

  1. Branch from main: feat/<area>, fix/<area>, docs/<topic>, test/<area>.

  2. Run checks locally (inside diskarte/):

    Terminal
    npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build

  3. Open a pull request against main. CI runs on PRs and on pushes to main only — pushing a feature branch alone doesn't run it.

  4. Merge with a merge commit (merge(<scope>): <summary>), keeping the branch's commits.

  5. After merging, Vercel deploys main immediately. Watch the CI run and load the production /login page before pushing anything else (see deployment.md).

Never force-push main or rewrite published history.

Commit messages#

Conventional-commit style, imperative mood, lower-case summary, scoped by area:

Text
feat(chat): built-in slash commands
fix(servers): name the channels relationship in the server list query
test(e2e): cover recurring announcement settings
docs(operations): add rollback steps for push
merge(community): slash commands, server rules and recurring announcements

Common types: feat, fix, perf, refactor, test, docs, merge. Put the why in the body when it isn't obvious. Don't add AI/assistant attribution trailers to commits or PR descriptions in this repository.

Pull request expectations#

  • One topic per PR; describe the user-visible change and how you verified it.
  • List any manual steps: migrations to apply, SQL installers to run, environment variables to set. Add them to diskarte/CHANGELOG.md and, if needed, a diskarte/RELEASE-<date>.md.
  • Include tests for new logic (see testing.md → Adding tests).
  • Update documentation in the same PR (checklist below).
  • Screenshots or short recordings for UI changes, including a phone width and light mode.

Coding conventions#

TypeScript

  • strict is on. Prefer inferred types; use z.infer for anything validated.
  • Validate every trust boundary with Zod (lib/schemas/*): action inputs, route bodies, query params, JSON from storage. Never trust a client-provided user id — the server uses the session.
  • Import with the @/ alias (@/lib/…, @/components/…).
  • Server-only modules import server-only; secrets are read only in those modules. A test fails if a "use client" module references a server secret.
  • lib/supabase/database.types.ts mirrors the schema; update it with new tables/columns/functions.

React and Next.js

  • Server Components by default; add "use client" only where state, effects or browser APIs are needed. Anything rendered from the root layout must be SSR-safe: create browser clients and touch window only inside effects.
  • Read runtime config through useSupabase() / RuntimeConfigProvider, never NEXT_PUBLIC_*.
  • Heavy UI (LiveKit, pickers, settings bodies, admin) loads lazily with a skeleton.
  • Realtime: use subscribeDbChanges() for Postgres Changes and always private: true channels.
  • Optimistic updates must roll back on failure and show a specific toast.
  • Follow the lint rules from eslint-config-next (core web vitals + TypeScript), including the React Compiler rules; justify any eslint-disable inline.

Style

  • The codebase is hand-formatted with long lines (~160 columns) and has no Prettier config — don't run Prettier over files; match the surrounding style.
  • Comment the why, not the what. Exported functions and components get a one-line JSDoc when their purpose or constraints aren't obvious from the name.
  • Known shortcuts are marked // shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade>.

Components

  • Reuse components/ui primitives (Button, Field, Modal, FloatingWindow, Popover, Menu, ContextMenu, Tooltip, ConfirmHost, EmptyState) and semantic CSS tokens. See UI, UX and design system.
  • Accessible by construction: real buttons/links, labels for inputs, keyboard support, 44 px touch targets, focus management through the shared overlays.
  • No emoji in UI chrome — add a glyph to lib/glyphs.ts.
  • UI copy is English, short and specific; add Filipino strings for navigation/settings to lib/locale.ts when you add those surfaces.

Database changes#

Read Database migrations and RLS review before touching supabase/migrations/.

Documentation#

Docs live in docs/ (product and engineering) plus runbooks in diskarte/docs/. Update them in the same PR as the code.

The Help Center (/docs)#

The public Help Center is rendered from the same Markdown:

  • docs/site.json lists the published pages, their URL slugs, sidebar sections and the reviewed date. Only listed pages are published; every other Markdown file under docs/ must be in its internal list (operational runbooks, the generated database reference, templates). The repository itself is public, so "internal" means "not on the website or in its search", not secret — never write secrets into any doc.
  • npm run docs:site --prefix diskarte renders the published pages to HTML (headings, anchors, highlighted code, method badges, Mermaid containers, rewritten links) into diskarte/src/content/docs-site.json and builds the search index diskarte/public/docs-assets/search-index.json. Commit both.
  • Links to published pages become /docs/...; links to code or internal pages become GitHub links. Raw HTML isn't allowed in published pages (the build fails).
  • Images live in diskarte/public/docs-assets/ and are referenced with a relative path from the Markdown. npm run docs:screens --prefix diskarte recaptures the product screenshots from the fixture harness (sample data only) and the production build, then rebuilds the site content.
  • In-app help links are defined once in src/lib/docs/help.ts. If you rename a heading they point at, the docs test tells you.
  • When you check a page against the code, update its reviewed date in site.json.

Docs checklist for a PR

  • New/changed feature → its page in docs/features/ (use the feature template) and the status table in docs/features/README.md
  • User-visible change → the relevant docs/user-guide/ page
  • New env var → docs/reference/environment.md and diskarte/.env.example
  • New route handler, action or error code → docs/reference/api.md
  • Migration → npm run docs:db --prefix diskarte (regenerates docs/reference/database.md), plus docs/database.md if the model changed
  • Architectural decision → an entry in docs/architecture/decisions.md (ADR template)
  • Manual deploy steps → diskarte/CHANGELOG.md / RELEASE-<date>.md and docs/operations/deployment.md
  • Limitation found or removed → docs/known-limitations.md
  • New Markdown page → publish it in docs/site.json or list it as internal; then npm run docs:site --prefix diskarte
  • UI the screenshots show changed → npm run docs:screens --prefix diskarte
  • Release users should hear about → an entry at the top of diskarte/src/content/releases.json (how)

npm test includes tests/docs/docs.test.ts, which fails on broken relative links or anchors in Markdown, a stale database reference or Help Center build, an unclassified or doubly classified page, an internal page or secret-looking string in the public bundle, an in-app help link to a missing page or heading, an API route handler missing from (or invented in) docs/reference/api.md, or an environment variable read by the code but missing from the environment reference. e2e/docs.spec.ts checks the site itself in a browser.

Writing style: plain, specific, present tense; explain why when it isn't obvious; real commands and paths; mark anything unverified as such. Diagrams use Mermaid (rendered by GitHub) and must describe the real implementation.

Troubleshooting your environment#

See troubleshooting → Local development.

developers/database-migrations.title: Database migrations and RLS review
developers/database-migrations.description: The schema is the security boundary, so migrations get the most careful review in this repository.
developers/database-migrations.html:
The schema is the security boundary, so migrations get the most careful review in this repository.

Rules#

  1. One file per change in supabase/migrations/, named YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_short_name.sql with a timestamp later than every existing file. Never edit a migration that has been applied anywhere shared; write a new one.
  2. Additive and forward-only. Add tables, columns, indexes and functions; replace functions with create or replace. Don't drop user data. Older app versions must keep working against the new schema, and new app code must tolerate the migration not being applied yet (hide the feature or show an "unavailable" state).
  3. Start with a comment block explaining what the migration adds and why. Put a -- comment directly above every create table and create function; the generated database reference uses it as the description.
  4. Portable SQL only. Migrations must run unmodified in PGlite (tests) and the CI Supabase stack. Anything needing pg_cron, pg_net or Vault goes in diskarte/docs/sql/*.sql as a reviewed, re-runnable installer.
  5. Applied by hand. Deploys never run migrations. Document every new file in the changelog / release notes with its order and what breaks without it.

Writing secure SQL#

SQL
-- Who may see a channel's pinned notes. Members only, private channels need a grant.
create table public.channel_notes (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  channel_id uuid not null references public.channels (id) on delete cascade,
  author_id uuid not null default auth.uid() references public.profiles (id) on delete cascade,
  body text not null check (char_length(body) between 1 and 2000),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
alter table public.channel_notes enable row level security;

create policy "members read notes" on public.channel_notes
  for select to authenticated using (public.can_view_channel(channel_id));
create policy "members write their own notes" on public.channel_notes
  for insert to authenticated with check (author_id = (select auth.uid()) and public.can_view_channel(channel_id));

-- Clears a note. Moderators of the channel's server only.
create or replace function public.clear_channel_note(p_note uuid)
returns void
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  if not public.has_server_role(public.channel_server_id((select channel_id from public.channel_notes where id = p_note)), 'moderator') then
    raise exception 'NOT_AUTHORIZED' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  delete from public.channel_notes where id = p_note;
end;
$$;
revoke all on function public.clear_channel_note(uuid) from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.clear_channel_note(uuid) to authenticated;

(An illustrative pattern — channel_notes is not a real table.)

Checklist:

  • RLS enabled on every new table, with policies to authenticated (anon gets nothing).
  • Use (select auth.uid()) (wrapped, so Postgres evaluates it once per statement).
  • Reuse the helpers: is_server_member, has_server_role, can_view_channel, is_dm_participant, is_platform_banned, is_verified_user, mfa_ok, is_super_admin.
  • Definer functions: security definer, set search_path = '', fully qualified names, re-check the caller inside, raise UPPER_SNAKE codes with a SQLSTATE (42501 permission, 23514 invalid, 53400 rate limit, 22023 bad argument).
  • Revoke explicitly. Supabase's default privileges grant EXECUTE on new functions to anon and authenticated. Revoke from public, anon (and from authenticated for internal helpers and trigger functions), then grant only what the app calls.
  • Server-assigned fields (author, timestamps, counters) are set by triggers, not trusted from the client. Guard immutable columns in BEFORE UPDATE triggers.
  • Rate limits for anything a user can spam (count recent rows in the trigger or RPC).
  • Realtime: add the table to supabase_realtime only if clients subscribe to it, and add the topic prefix to can_access_realtime_topic().
  • Storage: bucket file_size_limit and allowed_mime_types, object paths that encode ownership, and policies that check them.
  • Account lifecycle: decide what delete_my_account() should do with the new data (cascade or set null) and extend export_my_data() — wrap the existing functions as 20261029060000_account_data_coverage.sql does.
  • Embeds: adding a second foreign key between two already-related tables makes PostgREST embeds ambiguous (PGRST201); update app queries to use table!fk_name(...) hints.
  • Enums: a value added with alter type … add value can't be used in the same transaction; compare as text (see 20261013150000_forum_channels.sql).
  • Indexes for every foreign key you filter on and for policy predicates; note potential locks on large tables in the release notes.

RLS review procedure#

For each new or changed table, policy, trigger or definer function, the reviewer answers:

  1. Can a signed-out visitor (anon) read or call it? It should be "no" unless it's a deliberate public endpoint (like get_invite, username_available, post_webhook_message).
  2. Can a signed-in non-member see or change it?
  3. Can a member act on someone else's rows, or impersonate them?
  4. Can a moderator act on an equal or higher rank? Can anyone change their own rank?
  5. Does a private channel stay private through every path: table, search, Realtime topic, push, events, workspace?
  6. Does a banned, timed-out or MFA-pending session get refused where it should?
  7. Does a definer function leak existence (different errors for "not found" vs "forbidden") where that matters?
  8. What happens on account deletion and in the data export?

Each "no" needs a PGlite test that proves it (see testing.md → Database / RLS tests).

Workflow#

Terminal
# 1. write supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_<name>.sql
# 2. test it
cd diskarte
npx vitest run tests/db/<feature>.test.ts
# 3. update app types
#    src/lib/supabase/database.types.ts (or regenerate from a local stack:
#    npx supabase gen types typescript --local > src/lib/supabase/database.types.ts)
# 4. regenerate the reference (the docs test fails until you do)
npm run docs:db
# 5. optionally add a probe for the feature to scripts/check-database.mjs
# 6. record it in CHANGELOG.md / RELEASE-<date>.md

To see the current definition of a function after many migrations, query the catalog in a PGlite test (select pg_get_functiondef('public.fn'::regproc)) rather than reading old migration files.

Applying to a hosted project: deployment.md → Release procedure.
