api.html:
Diskarte exposes three kinds of interface:

  1. HTTP route handlers under /api/* and /auth/* — documented below with real request/response shapes.
  2. Server Actions ("use server" functions in diskarte/src/actions/) — called by React components, not a public API.
  3. Supabase PostgREST / RPC — the browser and server query tables and call functions as the signed-in user; RLS decides what they see. The full function list with signatures and who may call each one is in the database reference.

There is no public, versioned REST API for third parties. The only endpoint meant for outside callers is the incoming channel webhook.

Conventions#

  • Base URL: SITE_URL (production: https://diskarte-ten.vercel.app).

  • Authentication: Supabase session cookies (sb-*), set by sign-in. Route handlers call supabase.auth.getUser(); there are no API keys or bearer tokens for users.

  • CSRF: proxy.ts rejects non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS requests to /api/* whose Origin (or Referer) isn't the site's own origin or listed in ALLOWED_ORIGINS → 403 {"error":"Cross-site request blocked"}. Exempt: /api/livekit/webhook, /api/push/dispatch and /api/webhooks/<id>/<token> (they authenticate with their own secret).

  • CORS: only the site origin and ALLOWED_ORIGINS receive Access-Control-Allow-* headers (credentials allowed, GET, POST, OPTIONS, max-age 600 s).

  • Rate limits (per client IP unless noted; 429 with Retry-After):

    Scope Limit Configurable
    Any /api/* except health, LiveKit webhook, push dispatch 120 / min RATE_LIMIT_API_PER_MINUTE
    Auth form POSTs (/, /login, /signup, /forgot-password, /reset-password, /settings/account) 5 / min RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_PER_MINUTE
    Auth callbacks (/auth/callback, /auth/confirm) 20 / min RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_CALLBACK_PER_MINUTE
    Voice tokens 20 / min per user —
    Link previews and GIF search 60 / min per user (shared budget) —
    Voice previews 45 / min per user —

    Limits are in-process (per instance) unless UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL/TOKEN are set, which makes the proxy-level limits (api, auth, authCallback) shared across instances.

  • Caching: every authenticated response sends Cache-Control: no-store or private.

  • Errors: JSON { "error": "<human-readable message>" }. Messages are written for end users.

HTTP endpoints#

Method & path Auth Purpose
GET/HEAD /api/health none Liveness / readiness
POST /api/livekit/token session Mint a room token
POST /api/livekit/webhook LiveKit signature Voice preview invalidation
GET /api/voice-preview session Who is in a server's voice channels
GET/POST /api/push/subscription session Manage this device's push registration
POST /api/push/dispatch bearer secret Drain the push outbox
POST /api/webhooks/<id>/<token> webhook token Post into a channel
GET /api/unfurl session Link preview metadata
GET /api/unfurl/image HMAC signature Proxy a preview image
GET /api/gifs session GIPHY search
GET /api/admin/snapshot super admin Control Center data
POST /api/admin/releases super admin Publish, withdraw or republish a release announcement
GET /auth/callback — OAuth / email PKCE code exchange
GET /auth/confirm — Token-hash email confirmation
GET /auth/revoked — Clear a dead session cookie

GET /api/health#

Public, never rate limited, never redirected.

Terminal
curl -s https://diskarte-ten.vercel.app/api/health
JSON
{
  "status": "ok",
  "service": "diskarte",
  "version": "dev",
  "uptimeSeconds": 512,
  "timestamp": "2026-11-06T03:15:00.000Z",
  "checks": { "config": "ok", "livekitSecrets": "ok" }
}
  • ?deep=1 also calls Supabase Auth's /auth/v1/health (3 s timeout) and adds "supabase": "ok" | "unreachable" | "skipped". Deep checks return 503 when status is degraded; plain liveness always returns 200 so a container isn't restarted for an upstream blip.
  • version is APP_VERSION, else the first 7 characters of RENDER_GIT_COMMIT, else dev.
  • HEAD returns 200 with no body.

POST /api/livekit/token#

HTTP
POST /api/livekit/token
Content-Type: application/json
Origin: https://diskarte-ten.vercel.app

{"channelId":"6f1c…"}            // voice channel
{"conversationId":"0b9e…"}       // or a DM conversation (exactly one key)
JSON
{ "token": "eyJhbGciOi…", "url": "wss://example.livekit.cloud", "room": "voice:6f1c…" }

Errors: 400 invalid body / not a voice channel, 401, 403 (not a member, timed out, not a participant), 404, 429 (20/min/user), 503 (LiveKit not configured). Token TTL is 1 hour, scoped to the one room. Details: Voice, video and screen sharing.

POST /api/livekit/webhook#

Called by LiveKit Cloud. Body ≤ 64 KB; the Authorization header must be LiveKit's signed JWT (verified with LIVEKIT_API_KEY/SECRET, including the body hash). For participant_joined, participant_left, participant_connection_aborted, track_published, track_unpublished and room_finished on a voice:<uuid> room, it broadcasts an empty voice_changed event on the server's private server:<id> topic. Returns 204 (handled or ignored), 401 (bad signature), 413, or 503 (database/broadcast failure, so LiveKit retries). Needs SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY.

GET /api/voice-preview#

?serverId=<uuid> → { channels: PreviewChannel[], limited: boolean } where each channel has id, name, count, participants[≤8] { id, profile, muted, screen }, streamers[]. Requires membership, no platform ban, completed MFA; verification gates apply. 400 bad id, 401, 403, 429 (45/min), 503 (LiveKit/database unavailable).

GET /api/push/subscription#

JSON
{ "configured": true, "publicKey": "BNc…", "devices": [ { "id": "…", "device_id": "…", "label": "Chrome on Android", "created_at": "…", "last_delivered_at": null } ] }

configured is true only when all VAPID settings are present and push_ready() is true in the database. 401 signed out, 403 MFA pending, 503 push migration missing.

POST /api/push/subscription#

Body ≤ 8 KB, one of:

JSON
{ "action": "register", "device": "<uuid>", "label": "Firefox on Windows",
  "subscription": { "endpoint": "https://updates.push.services.mozilla.com/wpush/v2/…",
                    "keys": { "p256dh": "<87 base64url chars>", "auth": "<22 base64url chars>" } } }
{ "action": "test",   "device": "<uuid>" }
{ "action": "remove", "device": "<uuid>" }

→ { "ok": true }. The endpoint must be an allow-listed push vendor over HTTPS; the P-256 key is validated. Errors: 400 invalid, 401, 403 (MFA pending; not for remove), 413, 429 (PUSH_RATE_LIMIT from the database: wait a minute), 503 (push not configured).

POST /api/push/dispatch#

Internal: called by the database (pg_net) with Authorization: Bearer <PUSH_DISPATCH_SECRET>. The body is ignored — recipients and payloads come only from the database. Returns the batch counts as JSON, 401 (wrong secret), 503 (secret missing/shorter than 32 characters, VAPID/service role missing, or queue failure). maxDuration = 60 s. See background-jobs.md.

POST /api/webhooks/<id>/<token>#

The integration endpoint. An admin creates the URL in Server settings → Webhooks; the token is shown once (48 hex characters) and stored only as a hash.

Terminal
curl -X POST "https://diskarte-ten.vercel.app/api/webhooks/$WEBHOOK_ID/$WEBHOOK_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"content":"Build #42 passed ✅","username":"CI"}'
JSON
{ "id": "a7d3…" }
Field Rules
content Required string, 1–2000 characters (Discord-compatible name, so existing scripts work)
username Optional display name for this post (stored as webhook_name, ≤ 32 chars)
Status Body
200 { "id": "<message uuid>" }
400 Send JSON: {"content": "…"} · content must be 1–2000 characters · username must be text
404 Unknown webhook (bad id/token format, wrong token, deleted webhook or channel)
413 Body over 16 KB
429 Slow down: 30 messages a minute, Retry-After: 60
503 Couldn't post

Webhook posts have no author, can't ping @everyone/@here, and go through the database function post_webhook_message, which is executable by anon only and verifies the token hash. The proxy still rate-limits the path per IP (120/min).

GET /api/unfurl#

?url=<http(s) URL ≤ 2048 chars> → { "preview": { url, siteName, title, description, image, color } | null }. Fetched server-side through lib/ssrf.ts: default ports only, every resolved address must be public (checked at connect time to defeat DNS rebinding), redirects re-checked by hand, 512 KB and 5 s caps. image is rewritten to a signed /api/unfurl/image URL. Results are cached per instance for 1 hour (500 entries). 400 Link not allowed, 401, 429.

GET /api/unfurl/image#

?u=<image url>&s=<signature> — only URLs signed by /api/unfurl (HMAC-SHA256 with a key derived from LIVEKIT_API_SECRET). Returns PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP ≤ 3 MB with Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox, nosniff and a 1-day immutable cache. 403 bad signature or blocked host, 404 not an allowed image, 502 upstream failure. This exists because the CSP blocks third-party images.

GET /api/gifs#

?q=<≤50 chars>&offset=<n> (trending when q is empty) → { gifs: [{ id, title, preview, width, height, url }], next: number | null }. Pages of 24, rated PG-13. 503 when GIPHY_API_KEY isn't set, 401, 429, 502.

GET /api/admin/snapshot#

Super admins only (proxy and handler both check is_super_admin(); every RPC checks again). ?q=<≤64 chars> filters the roster server-side. Returns { overview, users, voice, audit, broadcasts, reports, traffic, generatedAt } in one round trip. 401, 403, 500 (migration missing).

POST /api/admin/releases#

Super admins only (proxy, handler and every RPC check). Body { "action": "publish" | "withdraw" | "reset", "id": "<release id from src/content/releases.json>" }.

Action Effect
publish Posts the release now (service role, same path as the automatic post); { "result": "published" | "already-published" | "superseded" | "failed" }
withdraw Deletes the post and keeps the record, so it isn't posted again automatically; { "result": "withdrawn" }
reset Deletes the post and the record, then publishes the current notes again

400 unknown release, 403 not a super admin, 503 migration missing, service role key missing or publishing failed. See release announcements.

Auth routes#

Route Behaviour
GET /auth/callback?code=…&next=… Exchanges a PKCE code (OAuth, email link, password reset) for a session, redirects to next (same-site paths only, via safeRedirectPath) or /login?error=…
GET /auth/confirm?token_hash=…&type=…&next=… For email templates using {{ .TokenHash }}; types signup, invite, magiclink, recovery, email_change, email; default next is /onboarding
GET /auth/revoked?next=… Signs out locally if a cookie is still present, then /login?error=Your session ended…

Server Actions#

All actions: verify the session (getSessionUser(), redirect to /login if missing), apply a per-user in-process limit (mutation: 60/min; message: 20/10 s), validate with Zod, call Supabase as the user, and return:

TypeScript
interface ActionResult<T = undefined> {
  ok: boolean;
  error?: string;                         // user-facing message
  fieldErrors?: Record<string, string>;   // per-field validation
  data?: T;
  code?: string;                          // machine-readable, e.g. "SLOWMODE", "AUTOMOD_BLOCKED"
  retryAfter?: number;                    // seconds (slow mode)
}
File Actions
app/(auth)/actions.ts signInAction, signUpAction, signInWithProviderAction, requestPasswordResetAction, signOutAction (all padded to ≥ 450 ms to blunt timing enumeration)
account.ts changePasswordAction, deleteAccountAction
profile.ts updateProfileAction, setStatusAction
messages.ts sendMessageAction, editMessageAction, deleteMessageAction, setPinnedAction, toggleReactionAction
social.ts sendFriendRequestAction, respondFriendRequestAction, removeFriendAction, blockUserAction, openDmAction, createGroupDmAction, leaveDmAction, sendDirectMessageAction, editDirectMessageAction, deleteDirectMessageAction
servers.ts createServerAction, joinServerAction, joinPublicServerAction, updateServerAction, deleteServerAction, leaveServerAction, transferOwnershipAction, createInviteAction, revokeInviteAction, regenerateInviteAction, createChannelAction, updateChannelAction, reorderChannelsAction, deleteChannelAction, setMemberRoleAction, kickMemberAction, setNicknameAction, createRoleAction, updateRoleAction, deleteRoleAction, assignRoleAction, setChannelAccessAction
moderation.ts updateAutomodAction, updateSupportAction, banMemberAction, unbanMemberAction, timeoutMemberAction, removeTimeoutAction, warnMemberAction, setBadgeAction, addSoundboardClipAction, removeSoundboardClipAction
voice.ts moderateVoiceAction (mute, unmute, deafen, undeafen, disconnect, move)
calls.ts ringAction, respondRingAction, cancelRingsAction
lfg.ts createLfgAction, joinLfgAction, leaveLfgAction, closeLfgAction
workspace.ts saveWorkspaceAction, deleteWorkspaceAction
reports.ts submitReportAction
admin.ts dispatchBroadcastAction, retractBroadcastAction, setRoleAction, overrideStatusAction, revokeSessionsAction, banUserAction, unbanUserAction, setReportStatusAction (super admins; each RPC re-checks)

Server Actions POST to the page URL, so the proxy's same-origin and auth rate limits apply to them too; Next.js additionally checks the Origin header for actions.

Database error codes surfaced to users#

Triggers and RPCs raise coded exceptions that actions translate (see messageError() in actions/messages.ts and communityError() in lib/community.ts):

Code Meaning
RATE_LIMITED 8 messages / 10 s across channels
SLOWMODE Channel slow mode; detail carries seconds left
AUTOMOD_BLOCKED Auto-mod dropped the message (insert returned zero rows)
VERIFICATION_REQUIRED Channel requires a confirmed email/phone
READ_ONLY_CHANNEL Only moderators may post
TIMED_OUT Member is in a timeout
RULES_NOT_ACCEPTED Server rules must be accepted first
POST_TITLE_REQUIRED Forum post without a title
INVALID_ATTACHMENT Attachment path/type/size rules failed
NOT_A_TEXT_CHANNEL Posting into a voice channel
ONLY_AUTHOR_CAN_EDIT, ONLY_MODERATORS_CAN_PIN, ONLY_ADMINS_CAN_CHANGE_ROLES, ONLY_ADMINS_CHANGE_PRIVACY, CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_ROLE, ONLY_OWNER_CAN_DEMOTE_ADMINS Guard-trigger permission failures
CONFIRMATION_MISMATCH Account deletion confirmation didn't match the username
WEBHOOK_NOT_FOUND, WEBHOOK_RATE_LIMITED Incoming webhook failures
PUSH_RATE_LIMIT Push registration/test throttled
PUSH_WAKE_NOT_CONFIGURED Vault secrets missing for push wake

changelog.html:
2026-11-08 — Hangouts, membership screening, suggestion boards, reminders#

  • Added Instant Hangouts: temporary group chats with a call for you and 1–9 friends, lasting 1–24 hours. Start one from Home, jump straight into voice and ring everyone; anyone adds an hour, the host keeps it, turns it into a Tambayan or ends it. Expired hangouts are deleted with their messages and take no file uploads.
  • Added friends who are around on Home: online friends first, their status and the voice channel they're in when you can see it. Invisible friends and anyone who turns off Settings → Privacy → "Show friends when I'm around" never appear.
  • Added membership screening: up to 5 joining questions and optional moderator approval, with a live queue in Server settings → Membership, a sidebar nudge for moderators and audit-log entries. Answers are included in the applicant's data export.
  • Added forum tags, Solved posts and pinned-first sorting, and suggestion boards with one-per-member upvotes, Top sorting and moderator statuses (Under consideration, Planned, In progress, Completed, Declined).
  • Added Remind me… on server messages: saved with a time and shown with a jump link (and a desktop notification when enabled) while Diskarte is open.
  • Needs four migrations: 20261108000000_hangouts.sql, 20261108010000_membership_screening.sql, 20261108020000_forum_tags_suggestions.sql, 20261108030000_message_reminders.sql. Existing features keep working without them; until they're applied the new actions fail with an error message.

2026-11-07 — smoother start, dependable notifications, release posts#

  • Fixed unread state missing a message sent within half a second of opening a conversation or of reading it (also the cause of the intermittently failing notification E2E journey): unread is now an exact comparison of database timestamps.
  • Fixed read DMs and channels coming back as unread on devices whose clock runs behind the server: receipts now cover the newest message shown.
  • Added a Getting started checklist and a What's New card on Home, with Filipino strings; a first-time greeting replaces "Welcome back" for new members.
  • Added official release announcements: each production deployment posts its developer-written release notes (src/content/releases.json) once to Diskarte HQ #announcements as "Diskarte Updates" with an Official badge; super admins can retry, withdraw or republish in the Control Center.
  • Added a plain-language Privacy and your data page, linked from the landing page, sign-up form and Help Center.
  • Needs migration 20261107000000_release_announcements.sql, then RELEASE_ANNOUNCEMENTS=on (Production only) with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, for the release posts. Everything else works without it.

2026-11-06 — Help Center#

  • Added the public Help Center at /docs: user guides, help and troubleshooting, the feature reference, developer docs, the API reference and this changelog, with search (Ctrl/⌘ K), section filters, breadcrumbs, an on-page contents list, previous/next links, copyable code, rendered diagrams, product screenshots, dark/light/system modes and a phone layout.
  • Added contextual help links in Settings (every section), server settings, the voice lobby, the shared workspace, an empty Tambayan and the sign-in page, plus Help Center links on the landing page.
  • Added "Suggest an improvement" on every docs page (signed-in feedback goes to the existing report queue; anyone can open a GitHub issue).
  • Updated zod to 4.6.7 (memory-exhaustion advisory) and added Mermaid 12 for diagrams; the production dependency audit reports zero vulnerabilities.
  • No database migrations or environment changes are needed.

2026-10-30 — community tools#

  • Added built-in slash commands in the composer: /shrug, /tableflip, /unflip, /me, /spoiler (Tab completes).
  • Added server rules: members accept them before posting (moderators exempt; editing them asks again), enforced in the database.
  • Added recurring announcements (Server settings → Announcements): daily or weekly posts at a local time, with last-failure reporting.
  • Needs two manual migrations; see RELEASE-2026-10-29.md (steps 8–9).

2026-10-29 — social, scheduling and integrations#

  • Fixed the mobile tab bar no longer matching the page colour behind the app (surface refactor regression).
  • Added favourite friends (listed first), custom statuses that clear after 30 min / 1 h / 4 h / 24 h, and mutual friends + shared Tambayans on member profiles.
  • Added scheduled messages in text channels (up to 30 days ahead, 25 pending per person) with a pending/failed list and cancel; they post as the author under the same rules as a live send.
  • Added Sent / Seen receipts under your latest DM (named readers in groups).
  • Added optional community levels per Tambayan: 15 XP per message at most once a minute, a leaderboard, levels on member profiles, admin reset.
  • Added incoming channel webhooks (Server settings → Webhooks) at POST /api/webhooks/<id>/<token>, hashed one-time-shown tokens, rotation, audit log entries and per-webhook + per-IP limits.
  • Added welcome messages for new members (channel + template with {user} / {server}).
  • Added optional Moments on Home: 24-hour text/photo updates for all friends or favourites only, with mute, report and delete.
  • Account export and deletion now cover favourites, scheduled messages, moments (incl. photos), mutes and XP.
  • Needs seven manual migrations and one optional cron job; see RELEASE-2026-10-29.md.

2026-10-15 — live voice activity and Web Push#

  • Added authorized LiveKit hover previews and mobile long-press sheets, with shared Realtime updates and signed webhook invalidation.
  • Added a private, transactional Web Push outbox, per-device session-bound subscriptions, leased dispatch, retries, event reminders, and invalid endpoint cleanup.
  • Prevented delayed push registration/reconciliation from restoring an account binding after logout; failed reconnects preserve existing subscriptions.
  • Added notification installation guidance, device management, synchronized delivery preferences, safe deep links, and private lock-screen defaults using the existing service worker.
  • Added queue/RLS, transport encryption, permission, worker-only browser, and interaction regressions; restored dialog focus as soon as dismissal begins.
  • Updated Next.js to 16.4.1, Sharp to 0.35.5 and source-map-js to 1.2.2; the production dependency audit reports zero vulnerabilities. ESLint’s unpatched development dependency advisories remain documented.
  • Push remains disabled until production secrets and the reviewed database setup are configured. See docs/web-push.md.

2026-10-14 — remaining-platform follow-up#

  • Added revisioned private draft/preference sync, private DM media, history anchors and reconnect reaction reconciliation.
  • Added community templates/settings export, discovery pagination, shared resources and saved collaborative whiteboards.
  • Added atomic event capacity, canonical RSVP summaries and finite weekly scheduling.
  • Added light/system appearance, core Filipino navigation/settings translations and time-zone preferences.
  • Improved keyboard viewport overlays and focus behavior; secured account export/deletion for newly persisted data.
  • Removed the AI report action/workflow while retaining manual reports and history.
  • Expanded migration readiness checks and multi-user browser regression coverage.

See the follow-up delivery report for exact results, migrations and unfinished scope.

2026-10-14#

  • Distinguished missing workspace migrations from connection, session and permission failures; added a read-only database readiness command and CI gate.
  • Added moderator event editing with concurrent-change detection, confirmed cancellation and timezone-safe calendar export; improved mobile form sizing, RSVP request deduplication and reconnect refresh.
  • Prevented abandoned conversation recovery requests and deferred bottom-scroll callbacks from affecting a later view.
  • Recovered missed event/RSVP deletion notifications with bounded, permission-checked refresh while Events is open; suspended polling for hidden, offline and closed views.
  • Added mobile destination tabs, keyboard-aware viewport, persistent call strip, swipe-to-reply and virtualized DM history.
  • Restored optional floating desktop panels and added a lazy keyboard navigation palette.
  • Added public community discovery, permission-aware global message search and historical message context.
  • Added channel-scoped shared notes, task boards and database-clock focus timers with concurrency checks.
  • Added safe PWA static caching, offline fallback, install/update controls, persistent local drafts, upload retry/cleanup, quiet hours and accessibility surface controls.
  • Fixed message retry identity, queue account isolation, concurrent rollback, cancelled call joins, muted rejoin behavior and reconnect history gaps.
  • Restricted private-channel events and RSVP visibility; added structured server errors and session-only connection diagnostics.
  • Expanded database, security, UI, concurrency, recovery, PWA and performance regression tests.

See delivery scope and limitations and migration/recovery operations. GitHub CI passed the full authenticated browser suite and Docker checks. The full platform master prompt is not complete; production migrations, live deployment, hardware testing and the explicitly listed product work remain pending.
